the-coal-blood.description: The coal-blooded: who carried the coal in their blood, and what became of them.

the-company.description: The humans' Company: its charter, camps, quays and coal ships.

the-mist.description: Manannan's mist, which hid the island from the ships beyond it, and its thinning.

events.title: The Crossing
events.body: Humans come ashore on Dia-thìr, bringing their Church with them, and are given leave to stay. They are the first strangers met since the Sundering.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The humans pray in a sail-loft at Cuan shean

events.title: The ships met off the north-west
events.body: That winter the mist that had lain on the eastern sea since the fleet of the Sundering sailed into it lifts from the northern water. Two fishing boats of Achadh àrsaidh, working the water off the north-west cape where the Sea-Watcher is seen, meet three ships coming down out of the thin grey from the north, and hail them; neither side understands the other. The fishers turn south and the ships follow them down the coast toward Cuan shean. The fishers call the place Coinneachadh nan Long, the meeting of the ships, and the boats of Achadh àrsaidh still slow there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The word brought home to Achadh àrsaidh

events.title: The word brought home to Achadh àrsaidh
events.body: The second of the two Achadh àrsaidh boats that met the strangers' ships off the north-west cape turns home and brings the word to its households, while Lachlann Odhar's boat leads the strangers' ships south toward Cuan shean. Achadh àrsaidh is the first place on the island to hear of the strangers, and it hears of them from its own fishers.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ships met off the north-west

told_in.book: Of the Gauze on the Water
told_in.section: II. Of the Gauze off the Cape

events.title: Three ships off Cuan shean
events.body: Three ships down from the north anchor off Cuan shean, the first hulls of their size seen from Dia-thìr since the fleet of the Sundering. Their master, a captain the rolls name Edmund Harrow, comes ashore unarmed with eleven men and asks by signs for water.

events.title: The rider from Cuan shean reaches Cathair dhearg
events.body: A rope-maker's son of Cuan shean rides the valley road to the capital in a day with Oighrig nic Leòid's letter on the ships. The clerk of the council reads it standing. The council's answer, two days later, bids Cuan shean feed the strangers, keep them apart and decide nothing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Forty days on the dunes

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Council of Custodians grants leave

told_in.book: Of the Gauze on the Water
told_in.section: III. Of the Empty Cask

events.title: Forty days on the dunes
events.body: The custodians of Cuan shean will not decide alone, and send inland to the capital for counsel. For forty days the strangers are fed on the beach and kept below the dunes.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The rider from Cuan shean reaches Cathair dhearg

events.title: The custodian of Baile fhiadhaich rides south
events.body: Word of the ships reaches Baile fhiadhaich, up the western coast, in two days. Its custodian rides south to see them, and writes to the council that the strangers' ropes are better than ours and their manners worse.

events.title: Oighrig nic Leòid's letter to the council from her sickbed
events.body: From her bed at Cuan shean Oighrig nic Leòid writes to the council that she gave the strangers water under the law of the shore and nothing more on her own word, and that a leave given in the roll cannot be ungiven. She asks that it be read before the vote. The clerk notes it received.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Council of Custodians grants leave

told_in.book: Of the Gauze on the Water
told_in.section: V. Of the Leave and the Margin

events.title: The Council of Custodians grants leave
events.body: The Council of Custodians at Cathair dhearg, which has sat in the crown's place since the crown fell empty at the close of the Age of Sundering, confirms the strangers' leave to stay under the high custodian Tormod mac Ailein. The council roll gives the vote as with one voice; a later hand in the margin notes that three custodians were absent.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The rider from Cuan shean reaches Cathair dhearg

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Oighrig nic Leòid's letter to the council from her sickbed

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The humans pray in a sail-loft at Cuan shean

events.title: The quarter of sea they came from
events.body: Old sailors at Cuan shean say that the strangers came in from the same quarter of sea the fleet of the Sundering sailed into. The council forbids the saying in its hall. It is written down all the same, and never answered.

events.title: The land beyond
events.body: The strangers name their homeland in their own tongue, but no scribe of the Dia-thìrich writes the word down. From the first season the scribes call it an Tìr Thall, the land beyond, and its people simply the humans.

events.title: The humans pray in a sail-loft at Cuan shean
events.body: On the day the strangers keep for their god a sailmaker of Cuan shean lends them his loft against the rain. They kneel on the sailcloth, the captain with the rest, while a priest reads from a book; they light no fire and burn nothing. Two priests of Manannan watch from the stair and go down to the water to say their own prayer. It is the first entry of the humans at prayer under a roof.

links.title: The Crossing

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Council of Custodians grants leave

told_in.book: Of Forty Words for the Colours of Coal
told_in.section: I. Of the Land Beyond

events.title: Wren and the priests come up to Cathair dhearg
events.body: Two priests of the humans and a boy ride up from Cuan shean on ponies of the town, a long day's road, and come over the bridge at dusk soaked through. The council lodges them in a house below the temple and gives them a long room on the east side of the hall. The younger priest, Samuel Wren, coughs in the damp of the lake country.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first attempts at speech

told_in.book: Of Forty Words for the Colours of Coal
told_in.section: II. Of Cup and Bread

events.title: The first attempts at speech
events.body: For a whole season clerics of the humans' Church and custodians of Dia-thìr labour to make a store of words in common. Neither side's account of what was agreed survives whole.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Wren and the priests come up to Cathair dhearg

events.title: Wren's word-lists
events.body: The human cleric Samuel Wren and the custodian Gormshuil nic Fhearchair keep word-lists side by side through the season of speech-making. Wren's list survives in the Administration's letter-books. Gormshuil's is lost; only its first leaf, with forty words for the colours of broken coal, is known from a copy.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muireall carries Gormshuil's papers to the loft at Muileann chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg

events.title: Muireall copies the first leaf
events.body: In the gap-moon Gormshuil nic Fhearchair gives her loose sheets to her niece Muireall to copy fair into a book for Clann Fhearchair, and orders the colours set first, before cup and bread, alone on the first leaf with room left at the foot. Muireall copies the forty words in her young, careful hand and stops at the right-hand column, where the humans' side has one word to give.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: One word for the coal

told_in.book: Of Forty Words for the Colours of Coal
told_in.section: IV. Of the Note under the First Leaf

events.title: One word for the coal
events.body: The humans have a single word for the coloured coal, and it is their word for the black fuel they burn at home. Gormshuil's copyist notes that no Dia-thìris word in either list answers to it, and that the humans did not ask for one.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Muireall copies the first leaf

links.label: Same person
links.title: Gormshuil given a copy of the terms

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg

events.title: Trade begins
events.body: At first the trade is fair on both sides: the goods of Dia-thìr for tools and knowledge the lonely island lacks. For a few years it seems it may last.

events.title: The trading post at Ros dhomhain
events.body: The humans set up a trading post at Ros dhomhain, the capital's harbour, and give iron tools, window glass, lamp-oil and paper for wool, salt fish, hides and dyed cloth. The first tally-book of the post, kept by the trader Thomas Pike, balances evenly through its first year.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pike writes home of the island's coal

events.title: The first hull on Loch chrom
events.body: Pilots of Caol leathan bring the first of the strangers' ships up the Abhainn gheal into Loch chrom, towing her with boats through the shallows below Baile ghlas, and she anchors off Ros dhomhain. Thereafter the humans' goods come to the capital shore by water, and the pilots charge a stranger's hull twice the toll of a Dia-thìreach boat.

events.title: Cathair naomh sends its wool
events.body: Cathair naomh, the city above Seann Toll on the northern coast, sends its first wool south to the humans' post by coasting boat. Its custodians take their payment in paper and ink, and with them begin the town's roll afresh.

events.title: Iron in the smithies
events.body: The smiths of Cathair dhearg take the humans' bar-iron gladly and learn to temper it in a winter. Within a few seasons the old bronze hoes are melted down for bells.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The ships' smith at the forge in Cathair dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gilleasbuig Gobha forges a hinge for Pike's chest

events.title: The ships' smith at the forge in Cathair dhearg
events.body: A smith off Harrow's ships, sent up by Pike, comes to the smiths' lane below the bridge at Cathair dhearg and works through the autumn at the forge of Gilleasbuig Gobha. Having no words in common, the two smiths agree on the colours of hot iron.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iron in the smithies

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: III. Of the Bar-Iron

events.title: Dyes for Baile Mòr mhòr
events.body: The weavers of Baile Mòr mhòr on the northern coast trade their cloth for the humans' dyes, a red and a blue brighter than any the island could make. Within a few years the old madder fields about the town go back to grass.

events.title: Harrow's second voyage
events.body: Harrow sails for home with hides and dyed cloth and comes back with four ships in place of three. He brings carpenters, a surgeon, and a letter from a trading house in an Tìr Thall asking what else the island has.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pike writes home of the island's coal

events.title: The shipwrights of Inis mhòr
events.body: The shipwrights of Inis mhòr come to look at the humans' hulls and measure them with knotted cords. Their guild had built nothing greater than a coaster since the fleet of the Sundering, and the old craft of building for deep water was half forgotten.

events.title: The surgeon Jonas Tull
events.body: The humans' surgeon, Jonas Tull, sets the broken leg of a fisherman of Cuan shean who had been given up as lame. The town's custodian enters it in the roll as the first debt owed to a stranger.

events.title: Salt from Seann Warr
events.body: The salt-pans of Seann Warr begin to sell to Pike's post by the barrel. They are the first goods of Dia-thìr that the humans come back asking for twice.

events.title: Wool at Caol leathan
events.body: The walled harbour of Caol leathan sends its first wool-ship to the humans' post. Its merchants will be paid only in iron by weight, and the tally-book of the post names them the hardest bargainers on the island.

events.title: Pike writes home of the island's coal
events.body: Answering the trading house, Thomas Pike writes of the island's timber, salt, wool, hides and smiths, and that it has copper, tin and some silver. Having held a piece from a custodian's hearth to the window, he writes that the island has coal of a middling sort, and much of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Harrow's second voyage

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The trading post at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: VII. Of the Middling Coal

events.title: Gilleasbuig Gobha forges a hinge for Pike's chest
events.body: Gilleasbuig Gobha makes a new hinge of the strangers' bar-iron for the iron-bound chest under Pike's counter, where letters for over the sea are kept. He tempers it to the blue and will take nothing for the work. Pike's letter on the coal goes over the sea in that chest.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iron in the smithies

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: VII. Of the Middling Coal

events.title: The first mixed settlement
events.body: A small coastal town takes in both Dia-thìrich and humans under one rule. It is not tried again.

events.title: Baile dhìreach under one council
events.body: The small port of Baile dhìreach on the south-west coast takes Dia-thìrich and humans under one council of six, three of each. Its founding compact is written twice, once in each tongue, the only such compact of the age.

events.title: The first council of Baile dhìreach
events.body: The council is chaired in alternate years by the fisherman Iain mac Chaluim and the human carpenter William Rook. The harbour dues go half to the custodians at Cathair dhearg and half to the humans' post.

events.title: Samuel Hale tightens the herring barrels
events.body: The human cooper Samuel Hale takes down the leaking herring barrels of Baile dhìreach stave by stave and makes every one of them tight by the end of summer, beginning with the idle row of the salter Ruairidh. He takes a bowl from the pot for his pay, and asks for Dia-thìris words, which he writes under his own.

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: III. Of Rope and Knot

events.title: The first boat off the humans' slip
events.body: On the first evening of Lùnastal the humans' slip at Baile dhìreach launches a small coaster of the strangers' pattern, deeper in the keel than the boats of the south-west. She is built for the fisherman Iain mac Chaluim, paid for in fish and labour and rigged with the town's rope; his wife pours sea water on her bow and asks Manannan to keep her.

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: III. Of Rope and Knot

events.title: A stranger's prayer at the lamps of the drowned
events.body: At the dark of the year Baile dhìreach sets lamps along its quay for its drowned, as the harbours of the west do. The humans of the shingle stand in the line, and the cooper Samuel Hale says a prayer to Crìosd in his own tongue for shipmates lost in the northern sea on the voyage out. Eilidh nic Ruairidh sets a lamp for them.

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: V. Of Her Father's No

events.title: Inis thais declines the compact
events.body: The city of Inis thais, whose harbour lies a few miles from Baile dhìreach, is bidden to join the joint council and declines. Its custodian writes that one town may be a trial, but two would be a rule.

events.title: A supply ship lost on the western reefs
events.body: A human supply ship strikes the reefs off the western coast in fog, and nine of her crew drown. Her master was sailing by a chart drawn from memory, the humans' letter-books complain, on a coast lit only by the old driftwood fires.

events.title: The beacons asked for
events.body: Human seamen, strange to the coasts of Dia-thìr, ask for standing beacons. The builders of the Dia-thìrich agree, not yet seeing what the beacons will bring.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pike writes of the natives

events.title: The beacon headlands walked
events.body: The human navigator James Fenn and the Dia-thìreach mason Torcall Clachair walk the coast together to choose the places of the new beacons, and mark the five headlands of the old fires. Fenn's chart survives; Torcall's cairns for the most part do not.

events.title: Pike writes of the natives
events.body: Thomas Pike enters in the post's letter-book that the islanders have agreed to the lights without difficulty and without asking what they would cost. It is the first page of his letter-book to call the Dia-thìrich the natives. The custodians' roll sets down the same asking as a request that the old sea-fires be built higher and kept all night.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacons asked for

told_in.book: Of the Five Headlands
told_in.section: II. Of the Asking

events.title: No fire on Binnean a' Chlachair
events.body: James Fenn asks for a night fire on the summit of Binnean a' Chlachair, the highest ground of the island. Torcall Clachair and the herders of Muileann gheal refuse, keeping the custom of the hills. Torcall lays one stone on the herders' cairn, and Fenn takes his sights by day to a linen square, four days slower. The two winter at Muileann gheal.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fenn's line

told_in.book: Of the Five Headlands
told_in.section: VI. Of Fenn's Line

events.title: Fenn's line
events.body: On the same survey James Fenn runs a line of sights across the whole island, from the open sea off the north-west, where ships coming down from the north first raise the land, to the water off the eastern cape. He makes it a hundred and fifty-five miles, some thirty of them sea at the western end. It is the first measure of Dia-thìr from side to side, and every chart the Company draws afterwards is scaled to it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: No fire on Binnean a' Chlachair

events.title: A marriage in two tongues
events.body: At Baile dhìreach the net-maker Eilidh nic Ruairidh weds the human cooper Samuel Hale. The council enters the marriage in both its books; the custodians at Cathair dhearg, asked for a ruling, send none.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall witnesses in the Dia-thìreach book

events.title: Torcall witnesses in the Dia-thìreach book
events.body: At the wedding on the quay of Baile dhìreach no custodian comes to witness. James Fenn signs for the bridegroom in the humans' book, and Iain mac Chaluim calls the mason Torcall Clachair from the crowd to sign the Dia-thìreach book. William Rook and Iain mac Chaluim close the two books side by side.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A marriage in two tongues

told_in.book: Of the Five Headlands
told_in.section: VII. Of the Two Books at Baile dhìreach

events.title: The first written treaty
events.body: The terms on which the humans stay are first set down in writing, in the humans' tongue only. No one among the Dia-thìrich speaks against it at the time.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ùna finds no silver in Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg

events.title: The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg
events.body: The treaty is signed in the council hall at Cathair dhearg by Tormod mac Ailein for the custodians, and for the Administration by Josiah Pell, newly come as the humans' first Commissioner. Tormod could not read the tongue it was written in. Who read it to him is not told.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Gormshuil called back from Muileann chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil given a copy of the terms

events.title: Gormshuil called back from Muileann chaol
events.body: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair, gone east with the season's copies for the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, is sent for by rider when the talks with Pell run fast. She starts back the day the rider finds her, but the rain is on the hills and the fords are up, and she is still on the road when the terms are signed.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Treaty in One Tongue
told_in.section: III. Of the Man Who Asked for a Horse

events.title: Gormshuil given a copy of the terms
events.body: Two days after the signing Gormshuil nic Fhearchair comes in from the hills, reads the entry in the roll standing, and asks Pell through Samuel Wren for the terms in the strangers' tongue, since the copy in Dia-thìris is to wait for leisure. Pell's secretary makes one within the week. She begins to read it a word at a time, and does not bring it before the council.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg

links.label: Same person
links.title: One word for the coal

told_in.book: Of the Treaty in One Tongue
told_in.section: IV. Of the Line Read Twice

events.title: The masons of the capital build for Pell
events.body: The masons of the masons' lane at Cathair dhearg take up Pell's house on the rise, paid in bar-iron by the humans' day, which begins at midnight where the island's begins at dusk. They float grey stone over the lake on rafts and build the house square to Pell's drawn plan, facing the harbour, with its back to the capital. The council does not ask it turned.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Residency above Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Treaty in One Tongue
told_in.section: V. Of the House on the Rise

events.title: The Residency above Ros dhomhain
events.body: Josiah Pell builds a house of dressed stone on the rise above Ros dhomhain and calls it the Residency. Captain Harrow, needed ashore no longer, goes back to the sea trade.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The masons of the capital build for Pell

events.title: The Company chartered
events.body: Harrow and Pike found a trading house under licence of the Administration, known on Dia-thìr simply as the Company. Its charter gives it first refusal of "all fuels, ores and minerals the island may yield."

events.title: The warehouse at Cathair dhomhain
events.body: The Company builds a stone warehouse at Cathair dhomhain, along the lake shore from the capital, to keep its tools from the harbour thieves of Ros dhomhain. It is the first building on Dia-thìr the Company owns outright.

events.title: The strangers' fever
events.body: A fever comes ashore at Cuan shean with a crowded ship and runs down the west coast. Ninety-one Dia-thìrich die, and eleven humans. The custodians shut the town to ships for a season, and Pell protests in writing.

events.title: The fever at Baile àrsaidh
events.body: The strangers' fever comes to Baile àrsaidh, a day's walk up the coast, and kills its custodian and both her sons. No humans dwell in the town at all, and the custodians of the west take note of it.

events.title: The fever turned back at Cnoc àrsaidh
events.body: At Cnoc àrsaidh in the south-west the townsfolk block the road with carts and turn back every traveller for a season, and the fever does not reach them. The Administration fines the town for hindering trade.

events.title: Prospectors in the central hills
events.body: The Company sends two prospectors, Abel Stone and Hugh Mercer, into the hills east of the capital. They come back with sacks of broken coal, and word that the black seam runs "further than can be walked in a day."

events.title: The sacks returned to the rock
events.body: The custodians of the vein demand the broken coal back, to lay it in the rock again with the proper words. The Company returns half. The custodians' roll enters the other half as "carried west."

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Six sacks come back to Muileann chrom

events.title: The first mining contracts
events.body: Trade sours into bargain. Dia-thìrich hands mine the vein on a scale that no reverent custom had ever used.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first contract read at the mill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall chosen to lead the thirty

events.title: The first pit at Muileann chrom
events.body: Under the first contract a Dia-thìreach crew of thirty opens a working at Muileann chrom, paid by the ton in iron tools and lamp-oil. The custodians' own cuttings had never been measured by weight at all.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall chosen to lead the thirty

events.title: Six sacks come back to Muileann chrom
events.body: At the summer's end a human carter brings six of the thirteen sacks back up the road to the mill of Muileann chrom with a paper no one there can read. Asked for the rest, he points west, towards Ros dhomhain and the ships, and turns his cart round.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The sacks returned to the rock

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: V. Of the Half Carried West

events.title: The first contract read at the mill
events.body: Abel Stone brings the first contract of A' Chompanaidh to Muileann chrom with two carts of steel-pointed picks, bar-iron and lamp-oil. It is read at the mill in both tongues. The interpreter from Ros dhomhain can find no Dia-thìris for the ton and calls it "a great load, weighed". Some of the older hewers walk out before the end.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first mining contracts

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: VI. Of the Contract and the First Ton

events.title: Raghnall chosen to lead the thirty
events.body: Abel Stone names Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, who walked the seam with him, to lead the first crew of the hill. The crew is thirty: young men of the hewers' and shepherds' households, two from the mill and three older hewers of the old cutting. Raghnall's father, a hewer of that cutting, will not join it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first mining contracts

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first pit at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: VI. Of the Contract and the First Ton

events.title: A coal quay at Ceann fhada
events.body: The Company builds a stone quay at Ceann fhada, a fishing hamlet below the hills, for loading coal into coasting barges. The fishermen are paid for their foreshore in iron nails, by weight.

events.title: Wren's grammar
events.body: Samuel Wren finishes a grammar of Dia-thìris for the Mission, the house of the humans' Church on Dia-thìr. It is careful and true in most things, and it gives the word for the vein's custodians as "keepers of the coal."

events.title: The hawk-priests read Wren
events.body: The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag ask the Mission for a copy of Wren's grammar, to read what the humans write of them. The Mission sends one. Of all the copies that survive it bears the most notes in the margins.

events.title: The Mission chapel
events.body: The Mission raises a timber chapel on the quay at Ros dhomhain, the first church on the island. Its bell is the first iron bell on the island, and the custodians ask that it not be rung before the fishing fleet is out.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The bell rung once before the fleet was out

events.title: The bell rung once before the fleet was out
events.body: On the morning of its hanging the iron bell of the chapel on the quay at Ros dhomhain is rung for the first service while the fishers are loading their boats in silence, as the rule of that quay requires. The crews unload and go home. Three boats of more than twenty go out on the lake that day.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Mission chapel

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: IV. Of the Bell before the Fleet

events.title: The first refusal
events.body: One mining settlement will not sign a contract. For the present it is passed by, not punished.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth

events.title: Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth
events.body: On the evening the day for the marks goes by, Beathag Dhubh calls the seven households of Doire mhòr to her fire and has the contract told to them. They talk of iron, oats and sheep. The oldest woman of the hill says that the hill is not theirs, and the households give the answer to the custodian to give.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first refusal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: V. Of the Paper at the Hearth

events.title: Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr
events.body: The settlement that refused was Doire mhòr, in the hills above Muileann chrom, and its custodian was Beathag Dhubh. Her answer to the Company's agent is known only in his words: that the hill was not hers to sell nor his to buy.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Dhubh dies at Doire mhòr

events.title: The road around Doire mhòr
events.body: The Company opens its next working at Cnoc fhiadhaich instead, and runs its cart-road round the fields of Doire mhòr and not through them.

events.title: Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg lit
events.body: The first of the new beacons is finished on the southern headland at Tobar dhearg: a round tower of grey stone raised over the old fire-tower, paid for by the Company, with a Dia-thìreach keeper. Torcall Clachair builds it; James Fenn sets its lens.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anna nic Dhòmhnaill's tally of lit nights cut on the stair wall

events.title: The first keeper of Tobar dhearg
events.body: The first keeper of the southern beacon is Anna nic Dhòmhnaill of Tobar dhearg village, a fisherman's widow, who climbs the tower twice a night for the rest of her life. The village holds the keepership as a trust and keeps it in its own families through the age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anna nic Dhòmhnaill's tally of lit nights cut on the stair wall

events.title: Anna nic Dhòmhnaill's tally of lit nights cut on the stair wall
events.body: Anna nic Dhòmhnaill, keeper of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, who cannot write, begins her count on the wall of the tower stair below the lamp-room: one stroke cut with a knife for every night the light is lit, and a stroke across every thirty.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg lit

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first keeper of Tobar dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Light at Tobar dhearg

events.title: Raiders in the north-western waters
events.body: A Company brig is boarded off the north-west coast and stripped of her cargo of tools. The raiders are never known. The Administration blames the custodians of the coast, and the custodians answer that those waters have always kept their own law.

events.title: The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied
events.body: Samuel Wren copies the writing on the obelisk near Cnoc bheag and sends it over the sea to the scholars of an Tìr Thall. No answer comes. The custodians tell him the stone is older than the Dia-thìrich and that none living can read it.

events.title: The first coin
events.body: The humans' coin is brought in beside the old barter, for ease, it is said. Within ten years nothing that needs a tool from over the sea can be had for anything else.

events.title: The mark and its hundred pence
events.body: The coins are struck at Ros dhomhain from silver and copper shipped from an Tìr Thall: the mark and its hundred pence. The first striking bears a ship on one face, and nothing of Dia-thìr on either.

events.title: Cathair mhòr refuses the mark
events.body: The market of Cathair mhòr, greatest below the hills east of the capital, refuses the humans' coin for a whole year. The custodians of the town give way when the Company's tool-sellers will not cross their bridge.

events.title: Two books at the capital market
events.body: At the market of Cathair dhearg the tool-sellers take only marks, while cloth and fish still go by barter. The custodians' clerks begin to keep two sets of books, and complain of it in both.

events.title: Wren's winter at Dùn thais
events.body: The masters of the druid school at Dùn thais receive Samuel Wren for a winter of disputation. He asks them why the vein should be holy; they ask him why his fuel should be burned. Neither telling of that winter names a winner.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Wren's letter home on the druids

events.title: Wren's letter home on the druids
events.body: From Dùn thais, in the last days of the year, Samuel Wren writes to the house of his order over the sea by the packet of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir. He sets down a tale the eldest master told at the hearth of a holy man's voyage west in a boat of hides, very like the voyage of Naomh Breandan as an Eaglais tells it, told from the other shore.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren's winter at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: IV. Of the Winter at Dùn thais

events.title: Drochaid Cathair dhearg rebuilt
events.body: Company masons rebuild in dressed stone the old bridge over Abhainn dhomhain at Cathair dhearg, wide enough for coal-carts to pass two abreast.

events.title: The Commissioner's carriage
events.body: Company wheelwrights build a closed carriage for Josiah Pell, and he drives in it over the new bridge from the Residency to the council at Cathair dhearg. It is the first carriage on the island. The custodians still walk to the council, and say so.

events.title: The Harbour Articles
events.body: A second compact, the Harbour Articles, fixes the dues and anchorages of Ros dhomhain in the Company's favour. Like the first treaty it is written in the humans' tongue only, and this time two custodians refuse to sign.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh

events.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh
events.body: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair passes the sheet of Puingean a' Chalaidh on unsigned, and tells Josiah Pell in his own tongue that she will not put her name under what she has read. Ailean Ruadh of Baile ghlas refuses with her. The council's roll names the two, the first custodians to refuse a writing of the strangers.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Harbour Articles

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fishermen of Baile ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: VI. Of Puingean a' Chalaidh

events.title: The fishermen of Baile ghlas
events.body: The fishermen of Baile ghlas, whose boats had anchored free at Ros dhomhain time out of mind, are charged anchorage under the Harbour Articles. They take their catch to their own small harbour and sell it there to anyone but the Company.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh

events.title: The northern concession
events.body: The council grants the Administration upland pasture in the north-west about Muileann àrsaidh, for human families who will not work in the pits. The grant is for grazing; the families build houses of stone.

events.title: Death of Tormod mac Ailein
events.body: Tormod mac Ailein, the high custodian who signed the first treaty, dies at Cathair dhearg. The council chooses Coinneach Glas of Ceann àrsaidh after him, who had never met a human before the Crossing and has dealt with little else since.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod mac Ailein buried at Cathair dhearg

events.title: Tormod mac Ailein buried at Cathair dhearg
events.body: Six custodians carry Tormod mac Ailein to the ground behind the council hall, with the bells of the capital ringing, and the mourners lay their stones on the grave going round sunwise. Josiah Pell walks up from the bridge-foot bareheaded to stand at the edge of the ground. Samuel Wren stands at the gate.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Tormod mac Ailein

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: VIII. Of Tormod's Burying

events.title: Harrow lost at sea
events.body: Edmund Harrow's ship does not come back from the crossing. The Company passes wholly into Thomas Pike's hands, and the humans' letter-books mourn Harrow as the man who found Dia-thìr.

events.title: The Small-Burning Law lapses
events.body: Centuries of measured burning end within one generation. The Law is never repealed; once its keeping no longer pays, it is no longer kept.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The council files the letter from Dùn dhearg

events.title: The last count at Doire mhin
events.body: The custodians of Doire mhin keep the old count of the Small-Burning Law, the measure of coal that might be burned in a year, one season longer than any others. They enter it in their roll with the note that no one asked for it.

events.title: A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg
events.body: Fionnghal nic Artair, a custodian of Dùn dhearg, writes to the council in defence of the Small-Burning Law, the only such defence that survives. She holds that the Law was never for the coal's sake but for the people, who would become whatever the burning made them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The council files the letter from Dùn dhearg

events.title: The council files the letter from Dùn dhearg
events.body: Fionnghal nic Artair reads her letter standing to the council at Cathair dhearg. Coinneach Glas thanks her and bids it kept with the rolls, and the roll enters it as read and filed. The same sitting grants the Residency leave to widen the road to Muileann chrom for the coal-carts.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Small-Burning Law lapses

told_in.book: Of the Law That Went Out
told_in.section: IV. Of the Filing

events.title: Murchadh Seabhag preaches at Seann Skell
events.body: At Seann Skell the hawk-priest Murchadh Seabhag preaches that Mòd, the Hungry Hawk of Acaill, starves those who eat faster than the land can feed them. The sermon is copied and carried to the camps, and it is the first writing of the Dia-thìrich that the Company's agents are told to seize.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Company's agents seize the hawk sermon in the camps

events.title: The hearths of Achadh naomh
events.body: The households of Achadh naomh, in the hills north of the workings, who keep Na Seann Spioradan, will not light their hearths with coal bought of the Company. They burn peat as their grandparents did, and their elders teach that coal burned for wages is burned without the ancestors' leave.

events.title: The Company's agents seize the hawk sermon in the camps
events.body: The Company's agents at Muileann chrom go from hut to hut through the crews' camp with a basket and take every copy of Murchadh Seabhag's sermon they find, eleven in one morning. One woman burns her copy on her hearth before them, and her name is written down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh Seabhag preaches at Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Law That Went Out
told_in.section: VI. Of the Peat Hearths and the Pumps

events.title: Burning by the cartload
events.body: The Company's furnaces at Muileann chrom burn coal by the cartload to drive the new pumps, and no heed is paid to the custodians' tally of what the hill may give in a year. Coinneach Glas's council asks that the tally be kept, and is sent a copy of the Company's accounts.

events.title: Henry Maddox Commissioner
events.body: Josiah Pell sails home to an Tìr Thall and does not return. After him comes Henry Maddox, bidden to double the yield, with a letter from the Company promising him a share of it.

events.title: The oaks of Cathair fhada
events.body: Maddox buys the oak woods about Cathair fhada for pit-props. The town had cut them sparingly for generations; they are gone within the working lives of the men who fell them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The last oak of Cathair fhada's own cutting

events.title: The last oak of Cathair fhada's own cutting
events.body: Before the Company's fellers come, the woodreeve of Cathair fhada and his men fell with axes the one oak the spring lot had fallen on, as the town had cut since the Holy Age, and plant six acorns in the ring of its roots. The fellers begin with long saws on the morning after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The oaks of Cathair fhada

told_in.book: Of the Law That Went Out
told_in.section: VII. Of the Oaks of Cathair fhada

events.title: The first deaths of haste
events.body: A tunnel worked faster than any Dia-thìreach crew would have worked it falls in and kills eleven. It is entered as an accident.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The eleven buried at Muileann chrom

events.title: The eleven buried at Muileann chrom
events.body: The eleven dead of the fall at Cnoc fhiadhaich are buried in the ground above the mill at Muileann chrom on the fourth day after the fall. Marsaili nic Sheumais, keeper of the old cutting for Taigh na Fèithe, reads their names at the graves and writes each into the roll with father, mother and hearth, and the place as under the wild hill.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first deaths of haste

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: III. Of the Eleven

events.title: The eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
events.body: The fall was at Cnoc fhiadhaich, in a gallery driven forward without the timbering the Dia-thìrich crews had asked for. The custodians' roll names all eleven dead. The Company's report names none, and calls the gallery "unsound ground."

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The eleven buried at Muileann chrom

events.title: The coughing sickness
events.body: A dry cough runs through the camps at Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich, worst among the boys who break coal at the pit-mouth, and thirty-eight die of it. The Mission's surgeon calls it a winter complaint. It lasts through the summer.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill at the pit-mouth

events.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill at the pit-mouth
events.body: Dòmhnall, the six-year-old son of the crew-leader Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, who had gone to the breakers' benches at Muileann chrom in the autumn, takes An Casad Tioram in am Màrt. He coughs nine nights on his father's knee and wakes well on the tenth morning, and goes back to the benches in the autumn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coughing sickness

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: IV. Of the Breakers at the Pit-Mouth

events.title: The orphans of Cill thais
events.body: The village of Cill thais takes in the children orphaned by the coughing sickness and keeps a house for them at its own custodians' cost. The Company, asked to give toward it, sends a crate of Mission primers.

events.title: Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit
events.body: The second beacon is lit on the eastern shore at Baile ìseal. Torcall Clachair, now too old to climb, directs its building from a chair at the foot of the headland.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall Clachair's last cairn

events.title: The keepers of Baile ìseal
events.body: The keepers of the eastern beacon are drawn from the fishing families of Baile ìseal. The town's custodians ask for a rule, and get it, that the lamp be lowered on the nights the boats go out to the deep grounds, lest the fish take fright. When the rule lapsed no one wrote down.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall Clachair's last cairn

events.title: Torcall Clachair's last cairn
events.body: Going home west from Baile ìseal in the spring after the lighting, Torcall Clachair has his cart stopped where the road tops the first rise of the moor and the tower first shows over the heather. Seated by the road, he lays a small cairn with his own hands from stones a boy brings from the ditch. He builds no more.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keepers of Baile ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: VI. Of the Light on the Eastern Cape

events.title: Seòlaid Ceann òg
events.body: The traders' boats from the new quay at Ceann òg go down the Abhainn ìseal past Cnoc bheag and Inis bhàn to the north coast, west along it, round the western capes, and south past Inis thais into the capital's water. Their lane is called Seòlaid Ceann òg after the quay. Off the north-west it swings far out into the open sea, and there the ships bound for an Tìr Thall leave it for the passage north-about, and the ships coming down from the north come in.

events.title: The camp at Àth ìseal
events.body: The Company builds a camp of timber huts at Àth ìseal, at the ford below the new workings, for crews brought in from the coast. It is the first settlement on Dia-thìr made for nothing but the pit.

events.title: Doire mhòr's water taken
events.body: The Company turns the stream that watered Doire mhòr to wash coal at Cnoc fhiadhaich. No order is written; the stream is dammed one season and not let go. Beathag Dhubh's people carry water by hand for two summers, and then begin to leave.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Dhubh dies at Doire mhòr

events.title: The short hunger in the hills
events.body: The men drawn from the farms into the pits, the hill villages of Muileann chrom lose their oats to rain, with none at home to cut ahead of it. The Company sells meal at the camp stores for marks, and the villages have few.

events.title: Muireall carries Gormshuil's papers to the loft at Muileann chaol
events.body: Muireall nic Fhearchair drives her aunt Gormshuil's papers east in a hired pony-cart to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, away from the reach of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir. Held by rain at Cuan chrom, she reads Clàr nan Dà Fhichead Dath aloud to the carter Seònaid Bhàn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren's word-lists

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: V. Of the Chest for the Loft

events.title: Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich
events.body: The villages of Doire fhiadhaich in the south send carts of meal north to the hill villages, as the old custom of the Holy Age bids in a hungry year. The Company's agents at Àth ìseal buy up two of the carts on the road.

events.title: The mountain dug by the ton
events.body: For the first time in the history of Dia-thìr the mountain is worked by the ton, and for ends no custom of the Dia-thìrich would have chosen.

events.title: Rope for the winding-gear
events.body: The rope-walks of Dùn chrom, which had made cable for the fishing boats, turn wholly to winding-rope for the pit-heads. The Company pays well, and the town grows by half.

events.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg
events.body: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg in the last days of an t-Sultain, in her seventy-first year. She had kept the council's list of the island's words since the ships came, refused to sign Puingean a' Chalaidh, and learned the humans' letters in her old age.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren's word-lists

links.label: Follows from
links.title: One word for the coal

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: V. Of the Chest for the Loft

events.title: The Company's second charter
events.body: The Company is chartered again in an Tìr Thall, with new money and a new name the Dia-thìrich never take up. Its agents at Ros dhomhain now outnumber the Administration's own clerks four to one.

events.title: Barges at Cidhe Beag
events.body: Coal barges begin to load at Cidhe Beag on Abhainn uaine and float the black coal down to the coast. The old canoe landing, used since before the Sundering, is widened with cut stone, and its shrine is moved uphill.

events.title: Abhainn uaine silts black
events.body: The washing of coal upstream fills Abhainn uaine with black slurry, and within a few seasons the salmon runs at its mouth fail. The river keeps its name, the green river, and the fishermen speak it bitterly.

events.title: Baile Mòr dhomhain a barge town
events.body: As the coal comes down to it from Cidhe Beag, Baile Mòr dhomhain on the river road grows into the busiest barge town of the north. Its people double in number, most of the newcomers bargemen from the coast.

events.title: Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair
events.body: Seònaid Bhàn, carter of Cuan chrom, marries Pàdraig mac Artair, a carter of Doire chaol. They live in her father's house at Cuan chrom beside the roofless carters' house at the quay, and their son Murchadh is born there the next winter.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: VII. Of the Green River

events.title: Baile dhomhain raised as a camp town
events.body: A Company surveyor lays out a second camp, Baile dhomhain, on a grid, the first town of the Dia-thìrich drawn on paper before it was built. Within two seasons it houses four hundred.

events.title: An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens
events.body: The old carters' house at the half-way stage of the coal road between the capital and the hills is built again, opens its doors at Lùnastal, and keeps the name An Taigh-seinnse Mòr. Its first keeper, Seònaid Bhàn, takes both marks and barter, the only innkeeper on the road who will.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair

events.title: Rathad na Mèinne
events.body: The Company's road-gangs finish metalling the carriers' road from Cathair dhearg by Doire chaol and the ford of Àth chiar to the workings at Achadh dhomhain, wide enough for coal-carts to pass both ways. The carters call it Rathad na Mèinne, the mine road. The posts with the crown's sign that had marked it since the Age of Sundering are left standing along it.

events.title: The carters of Doire chaol
events.body: The carters of Doire chaol, on the road just east of the capital, band together in a guild to bargain with the Company over the rates for hauling coal. It is the first Dia-thìreach guild of the age, and the Company owns it because that is cheaper than breaking it.

events.title: Seann Toll made a coal landing
events.body: The Company takes the river landing at Seann Toll, below the workings, and builds a loading stage there for the barges that carry the coal down the Abhainn uaine to Ceann leathan. The town's fishing boats are moved to the next reach.

events.title: The coal ships' lane
events.body: From the landing at Seann Toll the coal barges go down the Abhainn uaine to Ceann leathan, where the Company's ships load at the river mouth and go out by the southern lane, Slighe-mhara Caol fhiadhaich, west along the south coast to the wild strait and the open sea. The fishers of the south coast, who had used the lane for five hundred years, learn to keep out of the coal ships' way.

events.title: The first Dia-thìreach overseer
events.body: A Dia-thìreach is set over other Dia-thìrich miners, answerable to human masters. It is the first open crack within the Dia-thìrich themselves, and not only between them and the humans.

events.title: Raghnall Maor
events.body: The first overseer is Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill of Muileann chrom, a crew-leader who had worked the pits since the first contract. He is given the Company's staff and a house with a slate roof, and from the office the Dia-thìrich give him his byname: Raghnall Maor, Raghnall the steward.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall's slate-roofed house

events.title: Raghnall's slate-roofed house
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's masons from Ros dhomhain build Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a house of two rooms and a loft on common grazing above the mill at Muileann chrom, with glass windows and a roof of slate, the first slate roof in the town. The miller's wife names him Raghnall Maor as he goes by, and the crews take up the name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall Maor

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: III. Of the Slate Roof

events.title: The overseers multiply
events.body: Within a few years there are overseers at every working in the district, all Dia-thìrich, all answerable to the Company's agents. The custodians' roll no longer names them, and gives only their number.

events.title: Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr
events.body: Seumas Dubh, overseer of the new pits at Cnoc mhòr, is killed by his own crew after a boy is crushed on a haulage he had ordered hurried. The Company hangs two men at Ros dhomhain, the first hanging done by the Administration on Dia-thìr.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The two hanged named in the custodians' roll

events.title: The two hanged named in the custodians' roll
events.body: The roll of Cnoc mhòr names the two hewers hanged at Ros dhomhain for the killing of Seumas Dubh, Eòin Ruadh and Fionnlagh mac Aonghais, and records that their neighbours carried them home and buried them in the town's ground. The letter-book of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir gives them as two of the crew.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: V. Of Seumas Dubh

events.title: Hawk-priests barred from the camps
events.body: Henry Maddox bars the priests of Òrd an t-Seabhaig from the camps, for their preaching slows the work. The overseers enforce the order, though several of them are hawk-faithful, as the roll says. The Mission's chaplains, who keep a chapel in every camp, are not barred.

events.title: The pox at Ros dhomhain
events.body: A spotted pox comes ashore at Ros dhomhain on a Company ship and climbs the coal road into the camps. The Mission counts four hundred and six dead. The custodians count more, and write the difference in the margin of the Mission's list.

events.title: The pox in the south
events.body: The pox spreads south from the harbour to Baile chiar and the villages about it. The custodians there cut the names of the dead into the stone lintel of the council house, and they can still be read.

events.title: Baile dhìreach loses its harbour dues
events.body: The Administration moves its customs house from Baile dhìreach to Ros dhomhain and ends the sharing of the harbour dues. The mixed council, left with half an income, cuts its members from six to four.

events.title: Arthur Lisle Commissioner
events.body: Henry Maddox leaves Dia-thìr a rich man. Arthur Lisle, a lawyer, comes after him, and his first act is to have every compact since the first treaty copied into one bound book.

events.title: Beathag Dhubh dies at Doire mhòr
events.body: Beathag Dhubh, custodian of Doire mhòr, who sent A' Chompanaidh's agent down the hill, dies in her own house in an Giblean at sixty-one, among the few hearths left lit after the stream was taken. She is laid out with Doire mhòr's own coal at her head and feet, and the whole hill comes up to her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire mhòr's water taken

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Last Door at Doire mhòr

events.title: A customs house at Ros gheal
events.body: Lisle opens a second customs house at Ros gheal on the northern coast, where hawk-faithful fishing towns had traded with Company ships without paying dues. The customs officer is twice chased out of the town in his first year.

events.title: The silver of Muileann chiar
events.body: The humans seek to claim the silver seam at Muileann chiar as well. It is one of the few things the Dia-thìrich keep wholly in their own hands through all this age.

events.title: Ùna finds no silver in Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg
events.body: Reading the council's copies by rushlight at the inns of Rathad na Mèinne on her way home, Ùna nic Choinnich finds coal named on every page of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg and no word of silver, nor of any metal but the iron the humans paid with. At the inn below Muileann chrom she tells her grandson that A' Chompanaidh holds no paper for the seam.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first written treaty

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: III. Of the Council's Copies

events.title: Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild
events.body: The silver seam was held for the town by its guild of refiners, led by Ùna nic Choinnich. When the Company's surveyors came she met them at the adit with every member of the guild and all its ledgers, and bade them find the humans' name anywhere in either.

events.title: The Silver Compact
events.body: Arthur Lisle, reading the treaties closely, finds nothing in them touching silver. On Là Fhèill Brìde he signs a compact with the silver guild leaving the seam to the town, the first writing of the age in which the Dia-thìrich keep the better terms.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ùna locks the compact in the guild chest

events.title: The council's copies returned from Muileann chiar
events.body: In the spring after the compact Ùna nic Choinnich sends the council's leaves of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, Puingean a' Chalaidh and the pit contracts back to Cathair dhearg by her grandson Fionnlagh, wrapped in the same oilcloth they came in, with a bar of silver for the clerk who keeps the presses.

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: VI. Of the Guild Chest

events.title: Seann Bhral the silver port
events.body: The silver guild sends its bars to the sea by the old port of Seann Bhral and not by the Company's quays, and pays the port's custodians in silver for the use of it. The Company finds no ground in the compact to object.

events.title: The carters of Baile gheal
events.body: The carters of Baile gheal in the south-west take up the carrying of Seann Warr brine-salt round the lake to the capital, a trade the Company does not trouble to claim. It keeps the town's folk out of the pits for the whole age.

events.title: Ùna locks the compact in the guild chest
events.body: On the day Comann an Airgid reckons its year, the three keyholders open the guild chest and Cùmhnant an Airgid is read aloud in both tongues. Ùna nic Choinnich, aged fifty-nine, lays it back on the new book of weighings beside the notched boards of the old ledger, and the three locks are turned.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Silver Compact

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: VI. Of the Guild Chest

events.title: Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit
events.body: The third beacon is lit on the north-east coast at Àth dhearg. Its keeper, Tormod mac Pheadair, keeps a daybook of every ship he sees, and from his book the number of human sailings in these years is known.

events.title: Àth dhearg builds the tower
events.body: The masons of the beacon at Àth dhearg are its own townsmen, paid half in marks and half in the promise that the tower will guide their own boats home. Tormod mac Pheadair, the keeper, is one of them.

events.title: Pirates off the eastern coast
events.body: Raiders in low black boats take a Company coal ship off the eastern coast and burn her to the waterline, cargo and all. The Company says the silver guild paid them. The silver guild says nothing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keeper of Àth dhearg sees the burning collier

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keeper will not write the black boats

events.title: The keeper of Àth dhearg sees the burning collier
events.body: Two nights after entering a laden collier of A' Chompanaidh going south, Tormod mac Pheadair sees a red light low in the south under the cloud from the middle watch until near dawn, and writes that he does not know what it was. The carters bring word four days later that raiders have burned her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Pirates off the eastern coast

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: IV. Of the Glow in the South

events.title: The keeper will not write the black boats
events.body: In Dubhlas a clerk of A' Chompanaidh rides to Àth dhearg to read the daybook and asks the keeper to write in black raiding boats seen going south before the burning. Tormod mac Pheadair answers that he saw none and will write no boat he has not seen. The clerk reports the book of no assistance.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Pirates off the eastern coast

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: IV. Of the Glow in the South

events.title: The gunboat entered at Àth dhearg
events.body: In Teasach of the forty-seventh year a black two-masted ship of war of A' Chompanaidh, a gun in her bows under canvas and more men on deck than any trader carries, comes round the north coast and south past the cape. The keeper of Àth dhearg enters her with more care than any ship before.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A cove burned near Ceann leathan

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: V. Of the Gunboat and the Cove

events.title: A cove burned near Ceann leathan
events.body: A Company gunboat hunts the raiders to a cove near Ceann leathan and burns every boat drawn up on the shingle, most of them belonging to the town's fishermen. The raiders are not found.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The gunboat entered at Àth dhearg

events.title: The end of the joint council
events.body: The mixed council of Baile dhìreach breaks up in a quarrel over a boundary wall and never meets again. The human families go to Ros bheag and Ros dhomhain; the Dia-thìrich families stay. Households that were both split or fell silent, and which did which is not told.

events.title: The boatyard moves to Inis chrom
events.body: The human boatbuilders of Baile dhìreach move their yard to Inis chrom, a day's sail east, where the Company has promised them timber. The town takes them in without a joint council or any other compact, and within a generation they fade from its rolls.

events.title: The dry year in the east
events.body: For a single season the rain fails over the eastern farmlands about Achadh shean. It is a warning, and no one heeds it.

events.title: Baile ruadh loses its seed
events.body: At Baile ruadh in the east the drought kills the seed corn in the ground, and the town borrows seed from the Company's store at Seann Dunn, at a price paid back over five harvests. It is the first Dia-thìreach town to owe the Company a debt in grain.

events.title: Aonghas mac Coinnich's question
events.body: At Dùn thais the druid master Aonghas mac Coinnich puts to his students a question the school's register calls new: why the humans cannot see the colour in broken coal that every Dia-thìreach child sees. He does not answer it, and the register notes that he called it the wrong question.

events.title: The druid students of Baile Mòr uaine
events.body: Students of Aonghas mac Coinnich carry his question to Baile Mòr uaine and teach it in the town's hall of disputation. The hall's record of the argument runs to four hundred leaves, and ends, like his, without an answer.

events.title: Cathair gheal in the northern concession
events.body: The human families of the northern concession found a market town at Cathair gheal, with a stone hall for their magistrate and a chapel. The Administration issues its charter without asking the custodians.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann Mòr loses his seat

events.title: Eachann Mòr loses his seat
events.body: The council at Cathair dhearg protests the charter of Cathair gheal, which names no custodian, and receives an answer in the humans' tongue that none of its members can read with confidence. At the autumn choosing at Ceann àrsaidh the households put out Eachann Mòr, who has no letters of that tongue, and choose Dùghall Òg of the carting families, who worked five years at the Company's weigh-house.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cathair gheal in the northern concession

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The family of Eachann Mòr

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: IV. Of Eachann Mòr's Seat

events.title: Human farms at Cnoc ghorm
events.body: Human farmers of the concession clear land beside the Dia-thìrich village of Cnoc ghorm in the upland north-west, and build a mill. The villagers sell them grain until the mill is working, and then stop.

events.title: A fishing station at Ceann mhòr
events.body: A few human fishing families of the concession settle at Ceann mhòr, the harbour under the north-western headland. They are the first humans to fish the island's waters for a living and not for the Company's table.

events.title: The first Dia-thìreach child sent over the sea
events.body: One family, hoping for better treatment, sends a son to be schooled in the humans' homeland. He is never known to return.

events.title: The family of Eachann Mòr
events.body: The family that sent its son away was that of Eachann Mòr, a custodian of Ceann àrsaidh who had lost his seat on the council. The boy, Calum, sailed over the sea on a Company ship with a letter from the Mission and a purse of marks.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Eachann Mòr loses his seat

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The passenger line read at the Company's counter

events.title: The Mission school
events.body: The Mission opens a school at Ros dhomhain for Dia-thìrich children, taught in the humans' tongue. It takes thirty pupils in its first year, most of them overseers' children, and among them the Mission counts its first Dia-thìrich converts.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea

events.title: Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea
events.body: No letter comes from Calum by the autumn ships. In the winter Eachann Mòr writes to his son in Dia-thìris, pays a pupil of the Mission school to put it into the humans' tongue beneath his lines, and gives it with a mark to the master of the first ship going north. No answer comes to it, nor to the three he sends after it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The family of Eachann Mòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Mission school

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: VI. Of the Letters That Did Not Come

events.title: Schooling at Inis bhàn
events.body: The custodians of Inis bhàn in the north open a school of their own in answer to the Mission's, and teach the old reckoning, the rolls and the names of the hills. The Mission complains that the pupils come to its school the next year already knowing how to argue.

events.title: Tobacco on the concession farms
events.body: Human farmers of the northern concession plant tobacco on the sheltered slopes behind Ceann mhòr and sell the dried leaf to the Company's ships. Of the crops the humans brought, it alone is still grown on Dia-thìr.

events.title: Drochaid Ros fhionn
events.body: The Company rebuilds the old bridge over the river at Ros fhionn to carry the eastern coal road. While the carts run it is the busiest crossing on that side of the island.

events.title: Coal through Inis bheag
events.body: Coal from the eastern workings is carted over the new bridge and down to the river quays of Inis bheag, and goes by barge to Caol chrom at the river mouth for shipping. The Company deepens the river at the quays, and the town's old fish market is moved to make room for the coal stage.

events.title: Baile mhin ships the eastern coal
events.body: The river quays of Baile mhin, below Inis bheag on the Abhainn bheag, take the eastern coal that Inis bheag cannot load. The townsfolk are paid by the barge, and with the gain the town builds its first stone houses.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The passenger line read at the Company's counter

events.title: The passenger line read at the Company's counter
events.body: In the third year after his son sailed Eachann Mòr asks at the Company's counter at Ros dhomhain after the ship by name. She has come and gone twice since, under another master now. Against the day Calum sailed the clerk reads one line, a native boy, his fare paid in full, and says his book knows nothing more.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The family of Eachann Mòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile mhin ships the eastern coal

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: VI. Of the Letters That Did Not Come

events.title: Caol gharbh passed by
events.body: The coal road to Inis bheag passes Caol gharbh by a mile, and the town, which had hoped for the traffic, gets only its dust. Its custodians write that they had not known a town could be harmed by a road it was not on.

events.title: The thing in the north-western sea
events.body: The crew of a Company brig see a beast greater than their ship off the north-western headlands. The Administration's clerk files their report with the complaints about pirates, and the Dia-thìrich sailors of the coast say they had wondered when the humans would see it.

events.title: A brig lost in the mist
events.body: A Company brig bound for the northern landing with tools is caught by a gale in sea mist off Eilean fhada and driven onto the skerries. Her crew wade ashore at low water and walk to the harbour at Caol bheag. Thereafter the Company's charts mark the northern passage closed to its ships from midwinter to the end of spring, the season of the gales.

events.title: Whale-boats out of Àth fhionn
events.body: Human fishermen of the concession teach the boats of Àth fhionn to hunt whales with the hand-lance, and not wait for them to strand. The oil is sold to the Company for its lamps, and from this time whale-boats go out from the north coast every summer.

events.title: Surveyors lost at Doire uaine
events.body: Two Company surveyors go up into the hills at Doire uaine against the villagers' counsel and are not seen again. The Company sends a search party, which comes back after a day and will go no further.

events.title: The offerings at Doire uaine
events.body: After the surveyors are lost the villagers of Doire uaine leave salt and coal for the sìth at the foot of the hills, as their grandparents did after any death on the high ground. The Company forbids coal to be left lying and has the offerings gathered up, and the villagers leave salt alone.

events.title: The tithe raised
events.body: The share of mined coal taken by the humans' Administration rises steeply. What the Dia-thìrich receive does not rise with it.

events.title: Lisle's tithe schedule
events.body: The new schedule goes out from the Residency under Arthur Lisle's hand and raises the Administration's share from one part in five to one part in three. The custodians receive a copy in the humans' tongue, with a rendering made by a Mission pupil.

events.title: Weighing the grain at Dùn fhiadhaich
events.body: At Dùn fhiadhaich the tithe-gatherers begin to weigh grain as well as coal, saying the town's farms feed the pits and share in their gain. The custodians' roll calls it the tithe on the tithe.

events.title: The flux at Ros dhomhain
events.body: A bloody flux breaks out in the crowded quarters at the Ros dhomhain quays. The Mission's nurse, Anne Colby, makes a sick-house of the chapel, and it is said that she kept the dead below two hundred.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Company's surgeon visits once

events.title: The Company's surgeon visits once
events.body: The Company's own surgeon comes to the chapel door at Ros dhomhain, will not step past the threshold, and tells Colby she would do better to let the sick lie where they were found. He sends, before he leaves the harbour, a case of salts and does not come again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flux at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: III. Of the Sick-House in the Chapel

events.title: The flux reaches Seann Vell
events.body: The coal barges carry the flux to Seann Vell, the river port east of the capital on the Abhainn fhionn. The custodians of the town shut the barge landing for a season, and the Company fines them for it.

events.title: Walter Crane Commissioner
events.body: Arthur Lisle dies at the Residency of a fever of the heart. Walter Crane, who had been the Company's chief agent at the pits, is made Commissioner after him, the first to hold both offices one after the other.

events.title: The pay office at Ceann mhin
events.body: Crane moves the Company's pay office for the southern workings to Ceann mhin, and makes the crews walk there to be paid, a day each way, in place of sending the paymaster to them. The crews are not paid for the walk.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uisdean Ruadh's first walk to Ceann mhin

events.title: Uisdean Ruadh's first walk to Ceann mhin
events.body: Uisdean Ruadh, a hewer of Muileann chrom, walks with forty of his gang before light on a morning of frost to stand in the pay line at Ceann mhin till near dusk, and walks home again in the dark. He keeps the cost of it afterward on a notched stick, kept still by his family three generations on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pay office at Ceann mhin

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: VI. Of the Day's Walk to Ceann mhin

events.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor
events.body: Raghnall Maor dies, and the Company gives his staff to his son Dòmhnall. The overseer's office, which the custodians had hoped would die with the man, becomes a family's inheritance.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Maor buried beside the eleven

events.title: Raghnall Maor buried beside the eleven
events.body: Raghnall Maor is buried on the hill above Muileann chrom beside the eleven of his first gallery, in thin rain, with both shifts of the pit standing at the grave together, a thing not done for any death there before. Anne Colby stands at the grave's edge with her roll and adds, that evening, a line naming his office, the only such line the roll holds.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: VII. Of Raghnall's Burying

events.title: Taigh-solais Muileann bheag lit
events.body: The fourth beacon is lit on the northern shore at Muileann bheag, the first to burn coal and not oil. Its keepers say the flame throws a colour on the water that no oil lamp ever did.

events.title: The fishermen of Muileann bheag
events.body: The fishermen of Muileann bheag complain that the colour the coal flame casts on the water drives the herring off. The keepers do not change the lamp. Within a season the herring come back, and the complaint is withdrawn in a letter the Company keeps.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keeper's son answers Lowe on the point

events.title: The keeper's son answers Lowe on the point
events.body: Ailig's young son stands the watch beside Lowe on two further nights and tells him the colour is not a thing looked for but a thing seen, as rain is felt before it falls. Lowe records the boy's answer as the most honest, and the least useful, given him in eleven years on the island.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fishermen of Muileann bheag

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: I. Of the Coloured Flame at Muileann bheag

events.title: The dig at Làrach an Teampaill
events.body: The Mission cleric Edwin Lowe digs for a season at Làrach an Teampaill with Company labourers, seeking proof of an older faith on the island. He finds cut stone, burnt bone and marks he cannot read, and writes that the ruin's builders "were not the present race." The custodians agree, and add nothing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Griogal Odhar on Mòd and the older ground

events.title: Griogal Odhar on Mòd and the older ground
events.body: Asked whether any order of the island's faiths claims the ruin, Griogal Odhar tells Lowe that Mòd himself is said not to claim ground older than the vein, for a god who eats the hill can only eat what grew in the hill's own time. No order has ever asked for the ground, and none has been refused it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dig at Làrach an Teampaill

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: II. Of the Dig at Làrach an Teampaill

events.title: The pillar at Cnoc chiar
events.body: Edwin Lowe copies the writing on the pillar near Cnoc chiar and sets it beside Wren's copy of the obelisk at Cnoc bheag. He judges that the two scripts are not the same, and that neither is of the Dia-thìrich. His notes stop there.

events.title: The column at Cnoc ghorm
events.body: Lowe's last copy is of the column near Cnoc ghorm, and beside it he writes that its marks are like the pillar's, but not near enough to help. He leaves Dia-thìr the next year and takes his notebooks with him.

events.title: The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach
events.body: Peter Voss, a glazier left behind when his Company contract ended, builds a glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach and melts the white sand of Cuan ruadh with charcoal from the hills. It is the first glass made on Dia-thìr. Within a generation his Dia-thìrich apprentices carry the craft to the towns of the capital shore.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cairistìona nic Griogair sees the first pane

events.title: Cairistìona nic Griogair sees the first pane
events.body: Voss's fourth firing gives a pale green pane clear enough to see a gull through. His apprentice Cairistìona nic Griogair, who carried sand for him all that summer, laughs at the sight of it, the first laugh heard in the glass-house yard since the furnace was raised.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: IV. Of Voss's Glass-House

events.title: The silver guild refuses again
events.body: Martha Gale, an agent of the Company, offers the silver guild of Muileann chiar a partnership, on terms the guild's ledger calls generous. Ùna nic Choinnich, now very old, has the offer read aloud twice in the guild hall, and it is refused by show of hands.

events.title: The camp at Achadh dhomhain
events.body: A new camp is opened at Achadh dhomhain for the deep galleries under the hill, and within a few seasons it is the most crowded place in the district. Its houses are built of spoil.

events.title: Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar
events.body: The weavers of Dùn chiar take a Company contract for canvas for the camp tents and sacks for the coal, and the town thrives on it. Its custodians note that never before had the town made anything for a use it did not approve.

events.title: The first of the undying generation
events.body: A girl is born in the mining camps who takes more raw coal into her body over her life than any Dia-thìreach in living memory, and she does not age as the folk about her age. Her name is Aisling.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table

events.title: The coach to the camps
events.body: The Company puts a coach on the road between the quay at Ros dhomhain and the camps at Muileann chrom, twice a week each way, changing horses at the old waypoint houses. Clerks and overseers ride in it. The crews walk.

events.title: The coal weighed at the quay
events.body: The Company sets up a great steelyard at the Ros dhomhain quay, and thenceforth the island's yield is known by the ton and the hundredweight. The custodians' old count, kept in seasons of labour, is no longer entered in the roll.

events.title: Ros dhìreach the second coal port
events.body: The Company opens a second coal stage at Ros dhìreach on the southern coast for the workings south of the hills. Its first cargo is lost in a squall off the harbour mouth, and the fishermen moved to make room for the stage will not go out after it.

events.title: The nameless change
