events.body: What is befalling the child born two years before has as yet no name in any tongue spoken on the island. Decades pass before anyone tries to make one.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The women's rule of silence

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wash-house women first mark the child's stillness

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table

events.title: The women's rule of silence
events.body: Beitris Bhàn tells the women who sat the night of the telling that a charge laid on a man by a spirit is not theirs to spend on the camp's talk, whatever they make of the child in their own kitchens. No meeting is called and no vote taken, but the rule holds among them for years.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The nameless change

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: IV. Of the Child the Rolls Gave Three Things

events.title: The wash-house women first mark the child's stillness
events.body: Season on season the women who handle the camp's dying notice, before anyone else in Achadh dhomhain, that Aisling is not changing as a growing child should, and keep what they notice among themselves.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The nameless change

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: IV. Of the Child the Rolls Gave Three Things

events.title: The first steamer
events.body: The first ship driven by an engine comes into Ros dhomhain, a Company paddle-steamer out of an Tìr Thall. The fishermen row out to look at a ship going against the wind with no sail set. Within a generation the Company's coal goes out in nothing else.

events.title: The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table
events.body: At a laying-out in the camp's fourth winter, Donnchadh mac Thormoid's wife tells the sitting women, for the first time outside her own house, what her husband met in the deep gallery and what it charged him to keep, and what passed the night their daughter was born. She says the words are his and she will change none of them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first of the undying generation

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The nameless change

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: III. Of What the Wife Told the Women

events.title: The shrine at Cill dhìreach
events.body: At Cill dhìreach, a village at the edge of the workings, the custodians keep a small shrine where the pit crews leave the first piece of coal from each new gallery. The Company suffers the custom, for it costs a stone a gallery.

events.title: The keepers of Cill ghlas
events.body: The custodians of the shrine at Cill ghlas, in the hills among the workings, keep the old rites at the mouth of the oldest cutting while the Company's pits deepen about them. It is the last shrine in the district that the pit crews still visit on the old feast days.

events.title: A' Phlàigh Uaine
events.body: The Green Death goes through the mining camps. The coal dust is blamed, though no study of it is ever finished. Twenty-six settlements have cases.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anne Colby comes to Beitris Bhàn's door

events.title: The first cases at Achadh dhomhain
events.body: The Green Death is first marked at Achadh dhomhain: a greenish pallor, then a cough that brings up dark dust, then weakness. The camp buries forty in the first month, in a field beyond the spoil-heaps still called the green acre.

events.title: Twenty-six settlements
events.body: The sickness spreads along the coal roads from the camps at Muileann chrom, Àth ìseal and Cnoc fhiadhaich, and falls hardest on Ros dhìreach, Ceann òg, Inis ìseal, Baile dhomhain, Achadh fhada, Cnoc bheag, Muileann uaine, Cuan àrsaidh and Inis bhàn. The custodians' roll lists the twenty-six settlements that had cases, and leaves a blank line after the last, as though waiting for another.

events.title: The Green Death at Baile chrom
events.body: The Green Death comes to Baile chrom in the hills, not the town of that name in the north-west. The scribes keep the two apart with care, for in later tellings of the island's hungers they are confused.

events.title: Àth ghlas burns its huts
events.body: At Àth ghlas the custodians order every hut where a death has been burned with its bedding. The Company protests the loss of its property. The custodians note that the sickness stops sooner at Àth ghlas than anywhere else.

events.title: The dead of Cnoc naomh
events.body: At Cnoc naomh the dead of the Green Death are laid in the burial ground of the town's old shrine until it is full, and then in a field outside. The field is never ploughed again.

events.title: Walter Crane walks the sick-rows at Achadh dhomhain
events.body: Commissioner Crane walks the worst of the sickness's second summer at Achadh dhomhain and does not walk faster past the bad huts than the ordinary ones, a thing the custodians and Beitris Bhàn both note and remember afterward in his favour.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Walter Crane dies of the Green Death

told_in.book: Of the Green Death
told_in.section: IV. Of the Seal and the Letter-Book

events.title: Beitris Bhàn nails a feather over her own door
events.body: After laying out the fortieth body of the season, Beitris Bhàn nails a hawk's feather above her own door at Achadh dhomhain. The overseer's boy finds it and reports his father, and she pays the week's pay it costs her and nails up another within the month.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The camps turn to the hawk

told_in.book: Of the Green Death
told_in.section: V. Of the Feathers Over the Door

events.title: Doctor Bright's study
events.body: Nathaniel Bright, physician to the Administration, begins to study the sickness at Muileann chrom, weighing the dust in the lungs of the dead. In the second season of the work he falls ill, and his notebooks break off in the middle of a table.

events.title: Walter Crane dies of the Green Death
events.body: Commissioner Crane, who had walked the camps in the worst of the sickness, dies of it at the Residency. Martha Gale, the Company's agent at Ros dhomhain, holds his seal for the months until another comes.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Walter Crane walks the sick-rows at Achadh dhomhain

events.title: Anne Colby comes to Beitris Bhàn's door
events.body: Anne Colby, unsent by the Mission and unasked by any custodian, comes to Achadh dhomhain to learn from the layer-out Beitris Bhàn what her own hands have taught her of the Green Death. The two begin washing the camp's dead together, a custom the camp comes to call An Dithis a Nigh Còmhla.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A' Phlàigh Uaine

told_in.book: Of the Green Death
told_in.section: VI. Of the Washing

events.title: George Tolley Commissioner
events.body: George Tolley comes from an Tìr Thall with orders that the yield must not fall for the sickness. He does not visit the camps. His letter-book blames the dust, the Dia-thìrich custom of sleeping near the fire, and the custodians' shrines, in that order.

events.title: Quarantine at Caol mhin
events.body: Tolley sets a quarantine station at Caol mhin on the northern coast for ships from an Tìr Thall, and holds them offshore until their crews are looked over. It is the first order of his rule the Dia-thìrich approve, and they say so.

events.title: The camps turn to the hawk
events.body: The hawk-priests still barred from the camps, the crews carry their sermons in themselves. The overseers' reports of these years list hawk-feathers nailed above hut doors as a matter for punishment.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Beitris Bhàn nails a feather over her own door

events.title: Anne Colby's sick-houses
events.body: Anne Colby opens sick-houses at Àth ìseal and Achadh dhomhain and nurses there until the sickness ebbs. She is the only human the camp folk name in their own accounts of the plague, and they name her kindly.

events.title: Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe
events.body: Catrìona nic Eachainn, crew-leader of the seventh shift at Baile thais, asks the agent Silas Crewe to close the third and fourth galleries, where the Green Death struck worst, until the surgeon rules on the dust. Crewe answers that the yield must not fall on a physician's guess, and says only that he will write it up.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first strike

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The strike at Baile thais

told_in.book: Of the Eleven Days of Baile thais
told_in.section: II. Of the Agent's Answer

events.title: Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest
events.body: Asked by Catrìona nic Eachainn whether any old law binds a hill's rest, the custodian Sìneag of Baile thais searches her rolls and finds none: Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig governs the coal burned, not the coal cut, and no custodian before this age had needed to write a law about men sickening below ground.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first strike

told_in.book: Of the Eleven Days of Baile thais
told_in.section: III. Of the Coal-Tub

events.title: The huts of Cnoc gharbh
events.body: After the sickness the people of Cnoc gharbh, who had worked the southern galleries, leave their camp huts and go back to the old village on the hill. The next year the Company builds the huts again and brings in crews from the west.

events.title: The first strike
events.body: A whole mining settlement stops work for eleven days over conditions worsened by the plague two years before. The strike ends when the food, which the humans' Administration holds, runs out.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest

events.title: The strike at Baile thais
events.body: The settlement was Baile thais, below Cill ghlas, and the crew-leader Catrìona nic Eachainn called the halt after the Company would not close the galleries where the Green Death had been worst. For eleven days no coal left the town. On the twelfth the Company's store, the only store, was empty.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe

events.title: The Company's granary
events.body: After the strike the Company builds a granary of its own at Muileann chrom and forbids the camps to keep grain beyond a week's ration. The overseers enforce the order, and Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor signs it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìneag's rolls note a granary built against a stoppage

events.title: Sìneag's rolls note a granary built against a stoppage
events.body: The custodian Sìneag writes in her rolls that she has never before read of a granary raised to answer a stoppage rather than a harvest, and sets the words down as they stand, without further comment, for whoever should read the roll after her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Company's granary

told_in.book: Of the Eleven Days of Baile thais
told_in.section: III. Of the Coal-Tub

events.title: Fish smuggled from Ros gharbh
events.body: The fishermen of Ros gharbh carry salt fish up to the camps by night, past the Company's granary rule. The custodians' roll calls it the only trade of that decade that ran the right way.

events.title: Catrìona goes to the silver town
events.body: Turned out of Baile thais and refused work at every Company pit, Catrìona nic Eachainn goes east to Muileann chiar, and the silver guild takes her on as a refiner. The Company asks that she be sent back. The guild's answer was filed and has not survived.

events.title: The springs at Muileann ruadh
events.body: The Administration builds a new bath-house at the hot springs near Muileann ruadh for its officers mending from fevers. Dia-thìrich who had bathed there for centuries are let in on certain days, and charged a penny.

events.title: Three priests will not stand for the blessing
events.body: Three of the younger priests of Òrd Mhacha stand apart at the back of the temple hall rather than take their places for the blessing of the coin. Beathag Ruadh lets it pass unremarked before the Residency's clerk, and tells Fearghas mac Mhuirich only that the order answers for the rite done rightly, not for the road a rightly blessed thing afterward walks.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Macha's priests bless the coin

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Horses

events.title: Muileann chiar grows
events.body: The silver town grows beside the coal workings, for the humans want both, and the digging goes faster than the old reverence would ever have allowed.

events.title: Artair mac Iain seated after ten empty years
events.body: The Council of Custodians, unable to agree a head since Alasdair Liath's death, seats Artair mac Iain of the eastern shires as high custodian, six-and-fifty years old, in the hall where Tormod mac Ailein once signed the treaty. Fearghas mac Mhuirich says the order's blessing over him, both horses named.

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: II. Of the Seat Ten Years Empty

events.title: A second Muileann chiar
events.body: The silver trade crowds the old town, and the guild settles its refiners and carters in the coal-breakers' mill town to the west, which is called by the silver town's name from then on. The rolls call them the old town and the new, and do not always say which they mean.

events.title: Silver for marks
events.body: The silver guild begins to sell bar silver to the Company for marks, at a price the guild sets. It is the only ware on Dia-thìr in this age priced by Dia-thìrich hands, and the guild's hall fills with human coin.

events.title: Silversmiths at Muileann bhàn
events.body: Silversmiths settle at Muileann bhàn on the road to the silver town and live by working the guild's bar into ornaments for the humans' market. Theirs is the one Dia-thìreach craft sold in an Tìr Thall under a Dia-thìreach name.

events.title: Macha's priests bless the coin
events.body: At Tolley's asking the priests of Òrd Mhacha at Cathair dhearg, the order of the capital and the crown, bless the Residency's new coin. The priesthood of Macha teaches that the two horses of her rite, Dubh Sainglenn the black and Liath Macha the grey, each have their due; the dissenting priests say the coin is only one of them.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Three priests will not stand for the blessing

events.title: The Residency notes the order divided
events.body: Word of Fearghas mac Mhuirich's refusal reaches the Residency within the month. Tolley, near his own retiring, does not send for him; the Residency's letter-book records only that the order of Òrd Mhacha at the capital is divided on a religious nicety, and does not say what the nicety was.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The second change of coin

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: V. Of the Second Asking

events.title: The second change of coin
events.body: The barter goods of the Dia-thìrich are marked down against the humans' coin a second time, on terms the humans' Administration alone sets.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The Residency notes the order divided

events.title: Wool marked down at Baile Mòr fhionn
events.body: At Baile Mòr fhionn, where wool had been the measure of every bargain, a fleece is now worth by the Residency's table what a half-fleece was worth before. The town's weavers stop bringing wool to market and send it over the sea on their own account, until the Company refuses them freight.

events.title: The boats of Caol fhiadhaich sold
events.body: The fishing fleet of Caol fhiadhaich, unable to pay the new harbour dues in marks, sells half its boats to the Company. The men who sailed them go into the pits under the next year's contracts.

events.title: The dissenters go to Cnoc bheag
events.body: Priests of Macha who refused the blessing leave the capital's temple and settle in the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag. There they keep the older reading of Macha's two horses, and take in custodians who have lost their seats.

events.title: Iain Maor
events.body: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor dies, and his son Iain takes the overseer's staff. Iain Maor is the first overseer schooled at the Mission; he keeps his reports in the humans' tongue and his household in Dia-thìris.

events.title: The Levy
events.body: Tolley issues an ordinance, the Levy, by which every farming village in the west and north must send one in five of its able grown folk to the pits for two years. The villages are paid in marks, at the new rate.

events.title: Levy officers at Caol mhòr
events.body: The Levy's officers take their first tally at Caol mhòr in the north-west, reading the names of the chosen from a list in the humans' tongue. The custodians of the town write the names again in Dia-thìris, that they may know whom to look for.

events.title: The Levy in the north-west
events.body: The Levy falls hardest on the villages about Baile chrom and the northern concession, which had never sent crews to the pits. The Dia-thìrich of the concession are taken; its human farmers are spared.

events.title: The Levy read at Cnoc thais
events.body: The Levy's officers read their list at Cnoc thais, and the mason Dùghall Clachair hears his own name and his whole crew's called for the pits. Two days into the eastward march they are turned out instead to the headland at Baile chrom, where the fifth and last coast beacon is begun.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Building the last beacon at Baile chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The masons of Cnoc thais

told_in.book: Of the Levy and the Ring of Beacons
told_in.section: IV. Of the Masons of Cnoc thais

events.title: Baile ìseal sends its people
events.body: Baile ìseal sends forty-one of its people to the pits under the Levy, and nineteen come back when their term ends. The custodians' roll names the other twenty-two and the camps they were sent to.

events.title: Muileann naomh buys its way out
events.body: The custodians of Muileann naomh pay the Levy's officers in silver to halve the town's tally. The officers take the silver and the whole tally. The complaint is lodged at the Residency and filed.

events.title: The druid school's hall shut
events.body: George Tolley shuts the hall of the druid school at Dùn thais over a lecture on whether the humans' blindness to the coal's colour is a kind of sickness. The masters go on teaching in their own houses, to smaller rooms each year.

events.title: A gale strips the beacon's scaffold
events.body: A two-day gale out of the north-west tears the scaffolding from the third course of the rising tower at Baile chrom. Dùghall Clachair climbs the bare walls alone in the wind to judge whether the stone has shifted; it has not.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Building the last beacon at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Levy and the Ring of Beacons
told_in.section: IV. Of the Masons of Cnoc thais

events.title: The last disputation at Doire chiar
events.body: At Doire chiar, a village of the druid schools north of the eastern workings, the masters hold the last open disputation of the school on the eve of Bealltainn, in the open air on the village threshing-floor. Its matter is whether a question may be forbidden. The Administration's clerk who attends writes that it may.

events.title: Teaching in the sacred forest
events.body: Druid masters who may no longer teach in a hall begin to teach under the trees in the sacred forest of Flidais near Muileann chiar, where the Administration has no building to shut.

events.title: Building the last beacon at Baile chrom
events.body: Work begins on the fifth and last beacon, on the north-western headland at Baile chrom, with masons taken by the Levy from the very villages whose fields they leave untilled.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The Levy read at Cnoc thais

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A gale strips the beacon's scaffold

events.title: Uisdean mac Lachlainn named keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom
events.body: Uisdean mac Lachlainn of the headland villages is named the beacon's first keeper, on the recommendation of the very masons who built it: Dùghall Clachair among them, who signed the letter along with two of his crew.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit

told_in.book: Of the Levy and the Ring of Beacons
told_in.section: V. Of the Ring Made Whole

events.title: The masons of Cnoc thais
events.body: The Levy takes the masons of Cnoc thais to build the beacon at Baile chrom. Their foreman, Dùghall Clachair, cuts the names of his crew into the lintel of the lamp-room, the only writing on any of the five towers.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The Levy read at Cnoc thais

events.title: The five beacons complete
events.body: The ring of coast beacons is finished: Taigh-solais Baile chrom, Baile ìseal, Muileann bheag, Àth dhearg and Tobar dhearg. They serve a trade that is by now plunder in all but name.

events.title: Cuan ruadh loses its trade
events.body: The ring of beacons finished, the Company's steamers round the island without putting in, and within a few years the old coasting trade of Cuan ruadh up and down the eastern shore dies.

events.title: Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit
events.body: The beacon at Baile chrom is lit with a coal flame, and the ring is whole. The Company's ships can now round the island by night, and the keepers' daybooks show the sailings doubled within a few years.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Uisdean mac Lachlainn named keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uisdean begins to write beyond the weather

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uisdean's hand on the valve

events.title: Gorta Baile chrom
events.body: The Great Hunger follows a failed harvest across thirty-four settlements, made worse because the Levy has taken so many to the pits that too few are left to till the land.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first harvest short

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uisdean begins to write beyond the weather

events.title: The first harvest short
events.body: The harvest round Baile chrom comes in at less than half the carts of the year before, the fields sown thin for want of hands and beaten further by two summer storms. Uisdean counts the carts against his own earlier tally and finds the shortfall for himself.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gorta Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: I. Of the Empty Road

events.title: Baile chrom goes hungry
events.body: The hunger is worst at Baile chrom itself, whose people could see the new beacon from their empty fields. The custodians write that more died there than anywhere else, and the Administration, which kept its own count, does not gainsay them.

events.title: The famine country
events.body: The custodians' roll draws the bounds of the famine country along the north-west shore and the hills behind it. Within them lie Baile chrom in its own shire; Ceann mhòr, Àth fhionn and Àth dhearg in the shire of Ceann mhòr; Muileann àrsaidh in the shire of Cnoc thais; and Achadh àrsaidh in the shire of Muileann àrsaidh. Thirty-four settlements are counted within the line, and the roll gives the dead of each.

events.title: Uisdean begins to write beyond the weather
events.body: In his second spring keeping the daybook of Taigh-solais Baile chrom, Uisdean mac Lachlainn writes down more than the wind and the oil for the first time: that a farmer of his acquaintance ploughs alone, with none of the hands who worked beside him the year before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gorta Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: I. Of the Empty Road

events.title: The hunger at Doire ghlas
events.body: At Doire ghlas in the north the hunger takes the old and the very young first. The village sends its young folk to the camps for the Company's rations, and by the year's end it is half empty.

events.title: Inis mhin eats its seed
events.body: In the second winter of the hunger the townsfolk of Inis mhin on the north coast eat their seed corn. The Mission kitchen at the harbour feeds three hundred a day for a season.

events.title: The hunger reaches Seann Bhrenn
events.body: The hunger reaches as far east as Seann Bhrenn, where the custodians open the old grain-pits of the Holy Age, unfilled in living memory. They hold only dust.

events.title: The relief ship
events.body: A relief ship with grain from an Tìr Thall lies a month at Ros dhomhain while the Residency and the Company dispute who shall pay for its unloading. Meanwhile the Mission opens kitchens at Cathair gheal and Baile chrom, and Anne Colby, come back to the island, keeps the one at Baile chrom.

events.title: Uisdean's hand on the valve
events.body: In the second winter of the hunger, Uisdean mac Lachlainn climbs to the lamp of Taigh-solais Baile chrom and stands a long while with his hand on the oil valve, weighing whether to let the light fail. He writes the thought into the daybook and lets the lamp burn on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Levy set aside

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: I. Of the Empty Road

events.title: The Levy set aside
events.body: The Levy is set aside in the famine districts, too late for the harvest. It is not repealed. The custodians note that it was never used again, nor needed to be, for the villages had learned what it meant.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Uisdean's hand on the valve

events.title: Cnoc mhòr walks south
events.body: Rather than starve, the families of Cnoc mhòr in the north walk south to the camps and take work under the Company. Their village stands empty for a generation.

events.title: Robert Haskins Commissioner
events.body: George Tolley retires with honours. Robert Haskins, who follows him, orders that the custodians' council be consulted on the tithe, and then sets the tithe before the council has met.

events.title: Customs at Seann Dunn
events.body: Haskins opens a customs house at Seann Dunn on the eastern coast, and a Company store with it. The store sells the east its seed and its tools, and within a few years its ledgers hold the debts of half the district.

events.title: The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh
events.body: Custodians of nineteen settlements come in to Ceann àrsaidh through am Faoilleach, on foot and by cart, and camp along the inside of the town wall while they wait for the last of their number. Peigi Ghlas of Cill ghlas walks it in two days, carrying her cloak and her village's slate of the Levy's and the famine's dead rolled with it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first petition

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: II. Of the Store at Seann Dunn

events.title: The first petition
events.body: For the first time the custodians of the Dia-thìrich act together, and not settlement by settlement, and lay a written grievance before the humans' Administration. It is not answered.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh

events.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh
events.body: The petition was drawn up at Ceann àrsaidh by custodians of nineteen settlements, meeting for the first time as one body. Peigi Ghlas, custodian of Cill ghlas, carried it to the Residency and handed it to a clerk.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi Ghlas at the Residency

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Aonghas Ruadh's letters go unanswered

events.title: Peigi Ghlas at the Residency
events.body: Peigi Ghlas carries the fair copy of the nineteen settlements' petition to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir at Ros dhomhain, is turned back twice at the gate, and on the third day is shown into a stone passage smelling of lamp-soot to wait on a worn bench before a young clerk takes the paper, thanks her, and lays it on an unremarkable pile.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: IV. Of the Bench in the Passage

events.title: Aonghas Ruadh's letters go unanswered
events.body: Through the year after the petition is filed, Aonghas Ruadh writes twice more to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir asking only whether the paper of am Faoilleach was received and read. The first letter gets no reply at all; the second, in the autumn, is answered in a strange clerk's hand that the matter remains under consideration.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: V. Of Brìde's Lamp

events.title: Àth fhionn signs
events.body: Ruairidh mac Thormoid, custodian of Àth fhionn in the south-east, is the eldest of those who signed the petition. He was born before the humans' coin was struck, and says so beside his name.

events.title: Grievance first written
events.body: From these years come the oldest writings of grievance among the Dia-thìrich that survive. No hand is yet raised in them; yet in them it is first written that something has gone wrong.

events.title: Leabhar Baile thais
events.body: The oldest of them is a book of complaints kept at Baile thais, set down by many hands over some years: wages, deaths, the granary, the stream at Doire mhòr. The custodians' copyists call it Leabhar Baile thais.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Griogair mac Aonghais tells Fearchar to sing it

events.title: Griogair mac Aonghais tells Fearchar to sing it
events.body: Old Griogair mac Aonghais, who broke coal beside Fearchar's father before him, tells Fearchar that a column is for men who have given up hoping to be heard, and that he should sing the grievance instead of writing it. Fearchar carries the book back to Baile thais and begins working verses to the granary's short week.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Leabhar Baile thais

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: I. Of the Book That Would Not Stay Shut

events.title: The songs of Fearchar Bàrd
events.body: The poet Fearchar Bàrd, a breaker of coal at Muileann dhearg since boyhood, makes songs of the Levy and the famine, and they are sung in the camps. The overseers forbid them, and because they were forbidden several were written down.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar repays the docked wage

events.title: Songs at An Taigh-òsta Grianach
events.body: The songs of Fearchar Bàrd are sung in the roadside houses of the east, and An Taigh-òsta Grianach becomes known for them. The Company's carters sing them too, the keeper writes, not always knowing what they sing.

events.title: Fearchar repays the docked wage
events.body: Fearchar Bàrd walks to Baile thais to repay out of his own wage the boy docked half a week's pay for singing his song, and the boy refuses the coin, saying he would rather have sung it than not. The song is sung again within the week, further than before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The songs of Fearchar Bàrd

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: II. Of the Song That Was Forbidden and So Written Down

events.title: The Company's deep-water quay
events.body: The Company builds at Ros dhomhain a deep-water quay for the new iron steamships, which burn the island's own coal to carry it away. Fearchar Bàrd makes a song of that, the most quoted of all his songs.

events.title: The deep quay at Ceann chaol
events.body: A second deep-water quay is built at Ceann chaol in the south-east for the eastern coal. Its builders are brought from the coast, and the village of forty houses becomes a town of four hundred.

events.title: Baile thais walls its pithead
events.body: The Company rings the pithead at Baile thais with a stone wall and a gate, and pays a watchman to count who goes in. It is the first working on Dia-thìr walled against its own crews.

events.title: Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at the silver town
events.body: Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at Muileann chiar, a refiner of the silver guild to the end. The camp folk of Baile thais send men to her burying, and the Company docks each of them a day's pay.

events.title: The quay fire
events.body: A fire starts in the Company's coal sheds at Ros dhomhain and burns three days, taking two streets of the harbour quarter with it. The Company's inquiry finds no cause; the harbour quarter's own account has several.

events.title: The council without a high custodian
events.body: After the death of the last high custodian the Council of Custodians cannot agree on another, and sits for years with the seat empty. Robert Haskins writes to an Tìr Thall that this makes the council easier to deal with.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Artair mac Iain dies at Cathair dhearg

events.title: Artair mac Iain dies at Cathair dhearg
events.body: Artair mac Iain, high custodian for twenty and four years, dies at Cathair dhearg at eighty years old. Word of his death reaches Fearchar Bàrd on the road home from An Taigh-òsta Grianach, carried faster than either fire or song by a rider changing horses at every post-house.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The council without a high custodian

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: VII. Of the Fire on the Quay, and the Empty Seat

events.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean
events.body: The Long Drought lies on the island's dry season three years together, and bears hard on a people already worn thin by the tallies of the pits.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile chaol slaughters its herd

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coll's report names the drought-fever's true cause

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Every custodian of the drought country petitions Haskins

events.title: The wells of Achadh shean
events.body: At Achadh shean, whose name the drought bears, the wells fail in the second summer, and the cattle are driven west in a column the roll calls a day long. Fewer than half reach water.

events.title: The dry country
events.body: The custodians' roll counts ten districts of the east as drought country, worst at Achadh shean, Àth uaine, Achadh àrsaidh and Muileann chiar, and reaching down to Cuan ruadh and west toward Baile chaol. The Administration keeps no count of its own.

events.title: The cattle of Baile chaol
events.body: At Baile chaol the herds are slaughtered in the second summer of the drought, rather than watched as they die. The salt meat is sold to the Company for the camps, at a price the Company names.

events.title: Doire fhionn walks for water
events.body: At Doire fhionn in the east the women walk each day to the spring at Àth ruadh and back for water, half a day's journey. The custodians record it for the three dry years, and then cease.

events.title: Baile chaol slaughters its herd
events.body: With no grazing left within four days' driving, Baile chaol's custodian Ealasaid Ruadh orders the town's whole herd killed and the meat salted rather than risk the loss of it on the road. The town loses fewer of its people to hunger that winter than any other of the ten drought districts.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of the Long Drought
told_in.section: III. Of Baile chaol's Choice

events.title: Pilgrims at Allt an Àigh
events.body: The spring of Allt an Àigh, said never to have failed, runs on through all three dry years. Pilgrims who keep Na Seann Spioradan come to it from all the east, the first of them at Bealltainn, and the Administration sets a watchman to charge them for the water. He is called back after one season.

events.title: The pilgrims' road at Inis uaine
events.body: Pilgrims bound for Allt an Àigh gather at Inis uaine, and the townsfolk feed them freely, as the Old Spirits require. The town's own wells are low, and it gives away more water than it keeps.

events.title: Drought-fever at Baile Mòr ruadh
events.body: A fever of foul water follows the drought into the towns, worst at Baile Mòr ruadh, where the wells had been deepened into the old middens. Seventeen die. The Mission's report is the first to name the cause rightly.

events.title: The fever at Cnoc shean
events.body: The drought-fever spreads to Cnoc shean, whose one well is found tainted. The custodians close it, and for a year the town drinks from carts.

events.title: The Mission's wells
events.body: The Mission sinks deep wells at Achadh shean and Àth chrom with a boring-rig brought from an Tìr Thall, and they hold. The custodians of the east set down the Mission's wells and the Company's tallies on facing pages, without comment.

events.title: Coll's report names the drought-fever's true cause
events.body: The Mission's physician at Baile Mòr ruadh, a young man named Coll, tests the town's water and finds it fouled by the old midden ground its deep wells were sunk through. His report to the Mission's house at Cathair dhearg is the first that autumn to name the fever's cause rightly.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of the Long Drought
told_in.section: V. Of the Drought-Fever

events.title: Every custodian of the drought country petitions Haskins
events.body: Each of the ten drought districts' custodians petitions Commissioner Haskins in her own hand, unknown to the others, asking that the Company's quota be set aside until two seasons of ordinary rain are counted. Iseabail nic Leòid rides her own petition to the Residency and is told, as every other has been told, that the matter is under consideration.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of the Long Drought
told_in.section: VII. Of the Petition, Begun Alone

events.title: Achadh chaol goes to the pits
events.body: Their fields burned out by the drought, the people of Achadh chaol in the north-east go to the pits for wages, the first villagers of the eastern farm country to do so. Their custodian writes it down as the end of the village, not a flitting.

events.title: The tally not lowered
events.body: The coal tally is not lowered in the drought. The custodians of the east, their joint petition unanswered, each write to Haskins alone; to each he answers that the matter is under consideration.

events.title: The petition of Àth mhòr
events.body: Iseabail nic Leòid, custodian of Àth mhòr, writes the longest of the single petitions, forty pages listing her town's dead beasts. Haskins answers in two lines. Both survive, bound together by a later clerk.

events.title: The first inheritance of mixed blood
events.body: A suit over whether the grandchild of a marriage between a Dia-thìreach and a human may inherit the customary rights of mining is decided, and the Administration makes the ruling wholly to its own gain.

events.title: The case of Thomas Hale
events.body: The child was Thomas Hale, grandson of the marriage at Baile dhìreach of Eilidh nic Ruairidh and Samuel Hale, who claimed a share in a customary cutting through his Dia-thìrich grandmother. Oliver Dunstan, magistrate at Ros dhomhain, ruled that customary rights descend only through the line the Administration owns, and that it owns only its own.

events.title: Dunstan's rule applied
events.body: Within a few years Dunstan's ruling is used to pass eleven customary cuttings to the Company, each because some holder in the line had married a human or been born of one. The custodians stop entering such marriages in the roll.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mairead nic Aoidh stops entering marriages in the roll

events.title: Mairead nic Aoidh stops entering marriages in the roll
events.body: The custodian of Baile dhìreach ceases to enter marriages between Dia-thìrich and humans in her roll, judging that under Dunstan's rule such an entry has become a paper a family's enemies may use against it rather than one that protects anything.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dunstan's rule applied

told_in.book: Of the Law of One Line
told_in.section: V. Of the Eleven Cuttings

events.title: A cutting at Cnoc dhubh taken
events.body: Among the cuttings taken under Dunstan's rule is the old customary working at Cnoc dhubh, held by one family since the Holy Age. A great-grandmother of the line had married a human sailor; that is enough.

events.title: The Lamp-Watch
events.body: A fellowship of pit crews calling itself the Lamp-Watch begins to meet at Baile thais and Cnoc chaol under cover of a burial club. Its first known deed is to pay for the burying of an old breaker who had died in the Company's lock-up.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Griogair mac Ailein dies in the lock-up

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Thomas Hale sent for to read the surgeon's note

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Lamp-Watch's purse runs dry

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill given a seat at the Lamp-Watch's table

events.title: Griogair mac Ailein dies in the lock-up
events.body: Griogair mac Ailein dies in the Company's lock-up at Cnoc chaol of a fever the Company's own surgeon records as already advanced when he was taken. He has no family living to claim him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Lamp-Watch

told_in.book: Of the Law of One Line
told_in.section: VI. Of the Lamp-Watch and Griogair mac Ailein

events.title: Thomas Hale sent for to read the surgeon's note
events.body: Dòmhnall Ruadh, a crew-leader of Baile thais, carries a letter to Baile dhìreach asking Thomas Hale, known along the coast for his hard-won knowledge of the Administration's law, to stand at Griogair mac Ailein's graveside and read the Company surgeon's note releasing the body.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Lamp-Watch

told_in.book: Of the Law of One Line
told_in.section: VI. Of the Lamp-Watch and Griogair mac Ailein

events.title: Edward Vane Commissioner
events.body: Robert Haskins is called home after a quarrel with the Company over the price of steamship berths, and Edward Vane follows him. Vane is the first Commissioner born on Dia-thìr, at the Residency, and he speaks Dia-thìris, badly, but he speaks it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Vane speaks Dia-thìris before the council at Cathair dhearg

events.title: The tram-road to Ros dhìreach
events.body: Vane lays an iron tram-road, drawn by mules, from the southern workings down to the coal port at Ros dhìreach. It halves the cost of shipping coal, and ends the carting trade of the villages on the old road.

events.title: Vane speaks Dia-thìris before the council at Cathair dhearg
events.body: Edward Vane goes up to Cathair dhearg unsummoned and speaks three sentences of Dia-thìris to Comhairle a' Chùraim before finishing through the Mission's interpreter, telling the council he has come home. The clerk enters the word exactly, wrong tense and all.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Edward Vane Commissioner

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: I. Of the Man Who Spoke It Badly

events.title: The night-shift order
events.body: For the first time the digging is made to run without ceasing, day and night, and the mountain is given no season of rest at all.

events.title: The night crews at Cnoc chaol
events.body: The order falls first on Cnoc chaol, where the Company's newest galleries are opened to crews working by coal-lamp in two shifts. The custodians' roll writes that the hill was given no silence at all, and leaves the rest of the page blank.

events.title: The night-shift strike
events.body: The crews at Cnoc chaol refuse the night shift, and within a week are replaced by crews brought from the coast under the Company's new contracts. The Lamp-Watch keeps the strikers' families for a season, and then its money is gone.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Lamp-Watch's purse runs dry

events.title: The strikebreakers of Muileann dhomhain
events.body: The crews that replace the strikers at Cnoc chaol are brought through Muileann dhomhain, where the townsfolk turn them from every door. They sleep in the Company's barns, and several go home the next season.

events.title: The Lamp-Watch's purse runs dry
events.body: The Lamp-Watch, keeping the households of the crews who stood at Cnoc chaol, empties its purse by the second winter. Its own reckoning, kept in an unnamed hand, closes the year's account at nothing, and beneath it notes only that the hill was not given back its silence.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Lamp-Watch

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The night-shift strike

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Shifts and the Week It Lasted

events.title: Matthew Dunne's sermon
events.body: Matthew Dunne, the Mission's minister at Ros dhomhain, preaches against the night-shift order from the chapel pulpit, saying the Dia-thìrich are right that even the ground must rest. The Company complains to the Mission, and Dunne is called back to an Tìr Thall. The Lamp-Watch copies the sermon and reads it in the camps.

events.title: The lung-rot at Cnoc chaol
events.body: A wasting sickness of the lungs spreads among the night crews at Cnoc chaol and Baile thais. Unlike the Green Death it kills slowly. The Company pays the widows a pension for a year, then stops.

events.title: Iain Maor and the night shift
events.body: Iain Maor, overseer at Muileann chrom, writes to the Company that the night shift is killing his crews faster than it is paying for them. The letter survives because the Company filed it with his dismissal, which was undone a month later for want of anyone else.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Maor dismissed and restored

events.title: Iain Maor dismissed and restored
events.body: The Residency answers Iain Maor's letter with a notice relieving him of the overseer's staff for conduct unbecoming his office. His daughter Mòrag reads it to him by lamplight. Within a month, the crews having slowed the galleries to nothing, an unsigned notice restores him with no mention of the first.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Maor and the night shift

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: VI. Of Iain Maor's Letter

events.title: The coal line
events.body: The Company opens its railway from the pits at Muileann chrom down by Cathair dhearg to the deep-water quay at Ros dhomhain. Its engines burn the island's own coal, as the steamships do, and the tram-road to Ros dhìreach is left to the mules. Within a year the carters' guild of Doire chaol, which had hauled the coal on Rathad na Mèinne for eighty years, loses the long haul. From the first day the Dia-thìrich call the engine carbad-iarainn, the iron chariot, and the railway the coal line.

events.title: Coal-lamps from Baile ghorm
events.body: The potteries of Baile ghorm take a contract for clay lamp-bodies for the night crews, thousands in a year. The potters' own book notes that they are the first lamps made on the island for work in the dark by command.

events.title: Fionnan born
events.body: A second child is born bound to the coal as Aisling was, half a century after her. So it is known that the thing is no chance of one birth: it comes of the digging, and it will go on.

events.title: The Administration's count of the people
events.body: The Administration counts the people of Dia-thìr by district for the first time. Its figures for the humans are true to the household; for the Dia-thìrich they are rounded to the hundred, and in the hill districts to the thousand.

events.title: Cailean mac Eachainn taken on at the cellar
events.body: Cailean mac Eachainn, a turf-cutter's son of Muileann chaol with a plain hand at his letters, is taken on by the three households of the cellar when Seònag Bhàn's eyes fail her past close work. He is asked first not whether he can write fair, but whether he can hold his tongue.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodians' rolls at Muileann chaol

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: III. Of the Three Households

events.title: The district of the outer coasts
events.body: The Administration makes the outer coasts one district and rules it from the harbour office at Seann Vell on Eilean ruadh, where its revenue cutters lie: the islands of the west and south, Eilean bhàn with Cuan dhearg and Cnoc chaol, and the southern edge of the windy coast in the far north-west. Its surveyors walk to the edge of the great moss there, which no chain can cross, and go no farther. Beyond it the district map is left blank.

events.title: Seònaid nic Dhùghaill, last of the druid masters
events.body: Seònaid nic Dhùghaill, the last master of Scoiltean nan Draoidhean to teach openly in this age, dies at Dùn thais. No one is named after her, and the school's register ends with her death. It is taken up again only long after the humans are gone.

events.title: The custodians' rolls at Muileann chaol
events.body: The custodians of the east begin to send copies of their rolls for safe keeping to the town of Muileann chaol, which still kept Beathag nic Thòmais's loft of papers, beyond the Residency's reach. The copying is done in the houses of three families, and the copies kept in a cellar.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Cailean mac Eachainn taken on at the cellar

events.title: The second Muileann chaol
events.body: Some of the copies bound for Muileann chaol go by mistake to the smaller town of that name further north, and are kept there for years before the mistake is found. The custodians note that they were kept just as well.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Nothing of weight was lost

events.title: Nothing of weight was lost
events.body: By lamplight Fearchar mac Ailpein and Cailean mac Eachainn match the recovered northern rolls against the cellar's own patched record of the missing years, and find that little of any weight had truly gone missing, only kept for a time in the wrong cellar.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The second Muileann chaol

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: VI. Of the Copies Gone Astray

events.title: The word found at last
events.body: With two children now known, the custodians agree on a word for what is befalling them: fuil-ghuail, "coal-blood", rendered in the humans' tongue as coal-touched. It is meant as a physician's word. It outlives that meaning.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi Ghlas calls the custodians to Cill ghlas

events.title: The custodians who named it
events.body: The word was agreed at a meeting of custodians at the shrine of Cill ghlas, where the oldest cutting still stood open. They chose a plain word, fit for the physician's book. The roll gives the vote; who first put the word forward it does not say.

events.title: Peigi Ghlas calls the custodians to Cill ghlas
events.body: Peigi Ghlas writes to every custodian within two days' walk, calling them to the shrine of Cill ghlas on the night of the coming full moon to settle a name for the change that has now come twice upon a child of the pits, and asks the cellar to send a hand who can write it fair on the spot.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The word found at last

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: IX. Of the Naming

events.title: The Line of Aisling found
events.body: Cailean mac Eachainn, a copyist in the cellar at Muileann chaol, finds in the roll of the camp at Àth ìseal the marriage of Aisling's father, Donnchadh mac Thormoid, with his line written seven names back, as the custodians write a marriage. He carries the seven names up to Tobar dhìreach, to Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste, the last who says the lines, and she knows them for the line of Somhairle son of Ailean Mòr. She says Aisling's line to him backward, from her father to the mason who found the fire. So what the camps whispered at Aisling's birth is found to be true. Cailean writes the line in the margin beside her birth.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The third mark beside a birth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean walks to Tobar dhìreach

events.title: The third mark beside a birth
events.body: On the same page Cailean finds the birth of Aisling entered with a mark he has seen only three or four times in a year of copying, never explained in any book given him, and recognises it for the mark the camps' whisper had already fixed to one child in the settlement.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Line of Aisling found

told_in.book: Of the Line of Aisling
told_in.section: I. Of the Roll at Àth ìseal

events.title: Cailean walks to Tobar dhìreach
events.body: Rather than report to the cellar, Cailean walks the hill road to Tobar dhìreach with the seven names copied onto a scrap of paper inside his coat, to ask whether a line so old could truly be Donnchadh's own.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Line of Aisling found

told_in.book: Of the Line of Aisling
told_in.section: I. Of the Roll at Àth ìseal

events.title: The Administration's register
events.body: The Residency, hearing of the word, orders that any Dia-thìreach child showing the change be reported to the Commissioner's office. The custodians obey by reporting none.

events.title: Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas
events.body: Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas, her petition still unanswered, having trimmed Brìde's lamp herself the week before her death and said that she had asked the Residency once and meant to leave the asking there.

told_in.book: Of the Line of Aisling
told_in.section: V. Of the Staff at Muileann chrom

events.title: The third change of coin
events.body: The old barter of the Dia-thìrich is struck down as lawful payment altogether. Every bargain on the island now goes by the humans' coin.

events.title: The barter houses closed
events.body: The barter houses at Ros dhomhain and Cathair dhearg, where cloth and fish had changed hands without coin since before the Crossing, are shut by order. A clerk of the Residency writes that the ledgers are now "complete for the first time."

events.title: The fishwives of Inis mhòr
events.body: The fishwives of Inis mhòr, who had sold by barter at the river steps since before the Crossing, will take no coin for a week, in protest at the shutting of the barter houses, and give their fish away. The Company's clerks record it as a glut.

events.title: Marks borrowed at interest
events.body: Barter being struck down, the hill villages borrow marks at interest from the Company's stores to buy seed. Within a few years most of the villages of Muileann chrom owe the Company more than a year's crops.

events.title: The old market at Muileann òg
events.body: The old barter market at Muileann òg, where hill and coast had met to trade since the Holy Age, closes after its last season, and the ground stands empty.

events.title: Mòrag nic Iain Maor
events.body: Iain Maor dies, and his daughter Mòrag takes the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, the first woman to hold it. The Company approves her in a letter that calls her "a safe pair of hands."

events.title: Charles Merriman Commissioner
events.body: Edward Vane dies at the Residency. Charles Merriman comes after him with a small company of armed constables, the first standing force the Administration has kept on Dia-thìr.

events.title: The constable post at Muileann shean
events.body: Merriman's first constable post is built at Muileann shean on the northern coal road, a stone house with a yard for horses. The townsfolk call it the humans' second Residency, and do not mean it kindly.

events.title: Ruth Pallant teaches Hannah Webb the night watch
events.body: At Ceann mhòr, an old net-mender named Ruth Pallant tells the field-worker Hannah Webb of a night watch her own people's fisher-forebears learned from the island folk, kept in silence under a grey goose said to hold the sea shut. Hannah carries the telling of it home to the concession.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: II. Of Hannah Webb

events.title: Hannah Webb's first vigil
events.body: In a field behind her landlord's byre near Baile chrom, Hannah Webb keeps the silent watch for the first time, and sees, or believes she sees, a pale shape cross the night sky before she sleeps through a whole night for the first time in ten years on the island.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: II. Of Hannah Webb

events.title: The watch spreads along the concession's edge
events.body: Word of Hannah Webb's night vigil passes among the human labourers of the concession after a field hand sees her keeping it. Within a season a handful of others try it, and by autumn six or seven keep the field together on clear nights, spaced apart and silent.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: II. Of Hannah Webb

events.title: A barracks at Tobar ghorm
events.body: A second post is raised at Tobar ghorm, near the northern workings. The village's custodian is paid rent for the ground, and with it buys the village out of its debts to the Company store.

events.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom
events.body: The Mission at Cathair gheal reports that human labourers near Baile chrom keep vigil by night in the fields, praying in silence under the sign of a grey goose, which they call the wild goose of the Spirit. The Mission cannot find whence the practice came, and calls it irregular, a superstition learned of the Dia-thìrich. The Dia-thìrich of Baile chrom disown it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Ruth Pallant teaches Hannah Webb the night watch

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Hannah Webb's first vigil

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The watch spreads along the concession's edge

events.title: Manannan's priests on the grey night
events.body: The priests of Òrd Mhanannain at Ceann mhòr answer the Mission's report of the grey-night vigils. The practice owes something to the Dia-thìrich, they say, but to their own harbours and not to Baile chrom: the human fishing families of Ceann mhòr learned from them the night prayer to keep the sea shut, and the labourers inland keep it as a vigil of their Church, a night of silence under the wild goose of the Spirit in place of a prayer to Manannan. The priests call it Manannan's prayer gone astray, and do not admit its keepers to their house.

events.title: The dockers' strike at Ros dhomhain
events.body: The dockers of Ros dhomhain, Dia-thìrich and human alike, refuse to load coal for nine days over the new berth charges. It is the only strike of the age in which human workers stand with Dia-thìrich. Merriman's constables break it, and the human dockers are shipped over the sea.

events.title: Seann Vell's dockers stay out
events.body: The dockers of Seann Vell, the harbour next to Ros dhomhain, refuse to load the coal sent to them during the strike. When it ends they are not shipped over the sea, for there are no humans among them; but they are not hired again either.

events.title: Lorccan born
events.body: A third such child is born, in a mining town and not a camp; the thing is no longer bound to any one place.

events.title: Raghnall Breac walks to Cill ghlas
events.body: With his knees gone stiff for the low work at Baile thais and two grandchildren to feed, the ageing hewer Raghnall Breac walks two days to the new galleries at Cill ghlas, where the pay is better and the headings still stand tall enough for a man to work upright. He writes to his daughter Eilidh twice a year.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Blasting-powder at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Rending of Cill ghlas
told_in.section: II. Of Baile thais in the Winter

events.title: Cian born
events.body: A fourth is born within a year of the third. Never again do the children of the undying generation come so close together.

events.title: Blasting-powder at Cill ghlas
events.body: The Company begins to drive galleries under the hills about Cill ghlas with blasting-powder shipped from an Tìr Thall. The custodians of the shrine ask that no charge be set within sight of the old cutting. The Company's engineer marks their asking on his plan, and sets the charges below it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Raghnall Breac walks to Cill ghlas

events.title: Powder landed at Caol ìseal
events.body: The blasting-powder for the new galleries is landed at Caol ìseal on the northern coast, away from the crowded southern harbours, and carted inland under guard. The town's custodians ask what is in the barrels and are told it is lamp-oil.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill given a seat at the Lamp-Watch's table
events.body: The crew-leader Eilidh nic Raghnaill of Baile thais is asked, for the first time, to sit at the table where the Lamp-Watch keeps its business, and copies its minutes into a second book kept in her own linen chest, where no Company clerk would think to look.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Lamp-Watch

told_in.book: Of the Rending of Cill ghlas
told_in.section: II. Of Baile thais in the Winter

events.title: Scàineadh Cill ghlas
events.body: The Rending: in the hills east of the capital, about Cill ghlas, the earth tears open along a fault beneath a common working. Dozens are killed, and a whole mining district is shut for a generation.

events.title: The first open fight
events.body: A mining death, which the Dia-thìrich workers lay at the door of the humans' carelessness, leads to the first bloodshed between the two peoples.

events.title: The shrine at Cill ghlas lost
events.body: The Rending swallows the old cutting at Cill ghlas, where the custodians had kept the rites through all the age, and its shrine with it. The custodians' roll sets down the loss of the shrine before the loss of the dead; a later copyist has put them in the other order.

events.title: The district closed
events.body: The Company shuts the whole district of the Rending and fences it, leaving Cill ghlas, Àth chaol and their hamlets in the shires of Muileann dhearg and Muileann chiar without work. The villages empty toward Baile thais and Muileann dhearg, and the closed district is left to the thorn.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill at the fenced ground

events.title: The meeting on the moor road
events.body: The folk turned out of the closed district send their eldest to the custodians of Muileann dhomhain, who meet them at a standing stone on the moor road below the town, lest the Company's clerks see them in the town hall. At the stone the custodians lend them the land at the edge of the fenced ground. The place is called Coinneachadh an Fhearainn, the meeting of the land.

events.title: Achadh chaol raised by the dispossessed
events.body: Folk of the closed district build a new village at Achadh chaol, at the edge of the fenced ground, on land lent by the custodians of Muileann dhomhain. It is the only settlement of the age founded by Dia-thìrich for Dia-thìrich with no Company surveyor's hand in it.

events.title: The fight at Muileann chrom
events.body: The death that began it was a flooded gallery at Muileann chrom, where seven died after the pumps were stopped to save fuel. When the Company's agent came to the pithead the crews stoned him and his constables, and the constables fired. Four Dia-thìrich and one constable were killed.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill at the fenced ground
events.body: Eilidh nic Raghnaill walks to Cill ghlas to find her father's grave and finds instead the fence and the fallen headgear of the eighth heading. A constable turns her away from the closed ground. She writes nothing of the hour in the Lamp-Watch's book.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The district closed

told_in.book: Of the Rending of Cill ghlas
told_in.section: IV. Of the Fenced Ground and the Stone on the Moor Road

events.title: Mòrag Maor at the inquiry
events.body: At the Administration's inquiry into the fight the overseer Mòrag nic Iain Maor bears witness that the pumps were stopped on the agent's order. Her words are struck out. The Lamp-Watch gets a copy of them all the same.

events.title: The grey fever
events.body: A fever of the chest comes in on the ships and runs over the whole island, from the capital to the eastern farms. It kills the young and strong more than the old, the Mission notes in alarm. The camps, already hungry, bury more than the towns.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Buidhe's sister's boy dies of the grey fever

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins the burial club's book

events.title: The grey fever at Cathair mhòr
events.body: At Cathair mhòr the grey fever shuts the market for the first time in the town's memory. The custodians' roll gives the dead by street, and the longest list is of the street where the carters lived.

events.title: The grey fever at Dùn thais
events.body: At Dùn thais the fever takes the physician the Administration sent to treat it, and two of the Mission's nurses. The old houses of the druid masters are opened as sick-rooms.

events.title: Tormod Buidhe's sister's boy dies of the grey fever
events.body: A boy not yet old enough for his first wage dies of the grey fever at Baile thais under Eilidh nic Raghnaill's sitting, having asked her, near the end, what month it was. His mother keeps his name from the burial club's book, and Eilidh does not ask for it twice.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The grey fever

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: I. Of the Grey Fever

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins the burial club's book
events.body: Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins keeping a plain hand-written record for the burial club at Baile thais, answering to no custodian's roll, after watching her father Raghnall Breac carry twenty years of names in his memory and give none of them to paper. She means not to do the same.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The grey fever

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: I. Of the Grey Fever

events.title: The second petition
events.body: This one carries a threat beneath its words, not a plea. It is the first writing of the Dia-thìrich the Administration troubles to answer, and it answers with more guards, not with concessions.

events.title: The signatories of Cnoc dhìreach
events.body: Coinneach Ruadh, custodian of Cnoc dhìreach, signs the second petition, and in the same week is turned out of his post as clerk to the Company store. He is one of eleven who sign and lose Company work for it.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill
events.body: The second petition was drawn up by Eilidh nic Raghnaill, a crew-leader of Baile thais and one of the Lamp-Watch, and signed by custodians and crew-leaders of thirty-one settlements. It ends with a sentence the Residency underlined: that the hill would not be worked by people who were not asked.

events.title: The constables tripled
events.body: Merriman answers by tripling the constables and posting companies at Muileann chrom, Baile thais, Ceann fhada and Cnoc chaol, each with a walled store. The constables are paid from the tithe.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first constables' company reaches Baile thais

events.title: Barracks at Dùn chrom
events.body: A barracks for the constables is built at Dùn chrom, on the capital side of the hills, with room for two hundred men. For most of its first year it stands empty, for want of constables to fill it.

events.title: Ìomhar Seabhag
events.body: At Seann Skell the hawk-priest Ìomhar Seabhag preaches that Mòd's hunger has turned on those who have eaten the hill. The hawk-shrines of the west begin to serve as meeting-houses for the Lamp-Watch, and the constables do not yet know it.

events.title: The hawk-faithful of Ros gheal
events.body: At Ros gheal the hawk-faithful fishing families, who had chased out the Company's customs officers a century before, raise a shrine to Mòd on the harbour wall. The constables order it down. It is built again three times in a single season.

events.title: The hawk and the druids at Inis bhàn
events.body: At Inis bhàn the priests of the hawk and a few who still keep the questions of the druid school in private meet for a disputation, the first between them in living memory. It is written that it settled nothing, and that both sides afterwards signed the petition.

events.title: The grey fever in the north-west
events.body: The grey fever returns and settles in the north-west, about Baile chrom and the towns of the concession, where it kills humans as readily as Dia-thìrich. The Mission's hospital at Cathair gheal overflows, and for the first time Dia-thìrich and human sick lie in the same wards.

events.title: The first constables' company reaches Baile thais
events.body: Forty constables under an officer named Prosser march into Baile thais on the twenty-fifth of Gearran and wall the settlement's old open store within the fortnight, taking the camp's well inside the new wall. Eilidh nic Raghnaill and the burial club watch the company make camp on ground that had been common land that same morning.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The constables tripled

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: III. Of the Answer

events.title: Muileann fhionn shut in
events.body: Muileann fhionn, a Dia-thìreach mill town in the north-west, shuts its roads against the fever and keeps them shut for a season. Human carters of the concession are turned back with their loads at the town's edge.

events.title: The fever at Tobar fhiadhaich
events.body: At Tobar fhiadhaich in the north the fever takes one household in three. The custodians of the village burn no huts; they had heard of Àth ghlas in their grandparents' time, but judge it too late.

events.title: The road-houses make ready
events.body: The road-houses along the old mining roads begin to serve as waystations for bands of armed men. The roads make ready for a war not yet declared.

events.title: An Taigh-seinnse Òir
events.body: An Taigh-seinnse Òir, the great house on the eastern road beyond Dùn dhearg, digs a well in its yard and builds a wall round the well. The keeper tells the Company's carters it is against thieves.

events.title: An Leòmhann Buidhe
events.body: An Leòmhann Buidhe, the road-house on the northern road through the druid country, takes on six new ostlers in a single season, none of whom know anything of horses.

events.title: An Taigh-òsta Grianach walled
events.body: An Taigh-òsta Grianach, called the singing house since the songs of Fearchar Bàrd, raises a wall round its yard and sets a watch on its gate.

events.title: Am Buabhall Fortanach barred
events.body: Am Buabhall Fortanach, the great road-house on the south-western road, bars its gates at dusk and keeps a watch on the roof. Its keeper, Tormod Buabhall, keeps a list of travellers and sends it up the road each week, to whom is not told.

events.title: The harbour of Doire shean
events.body: The little harbour of Doire shean, below Am Buabhall Fortanach, becomes the landing for the goods the house cannot take by road. The fishermen of Doire shean are paid in silver from the east.

events.title: An Taigh-seinnse Reòta
events.body: At An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the northern road the stables are rebuilt with a loft for sleeping men. The Company's carters mark that the loft is never empty, and never holds the same men twice.

events.title: An Sligeanach Fad' às
events.body: An Sligeanach Fad' às, on the eastern road near the silver country, becomes the post-house through which the Lamp-Watch sends word from the camps to Muileann chiar. The silver guild pays its keeper's rent.

events.title: The runners of Àth fhiadhaich
events.body: Runners from Àth fhiadhaich carry the Lamp-Watch's letters from An Sligeanach Fad' às to the silver town. They are boys of twelve and thirteen, too young for the constables to stop.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A boy of Àth fhiadhaich at Aonghas's door

events.title: A boy of Àth fhiadhaich at Aonghas's door
events.body: A boy runner out of Àth fhiadhaich comes soaked from the ford into Aonghas's yard, asks for bread as any boy might, and leaves a folded scrap under the loose board by the stable door naming a date and nothing else. Aonghas burns it in the kitchen fire that night.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The runners of Àth fhiadhaich

told_in.book: Of the Houses on the Roads
told_in.section: III. Of the Post at the Far Shore and the Boys of the Ford

events.title: Achadh mhòr keeps the ledgers
events.body: The Lamp-Watch's ledgers of the money it has from the silver guild are kept at Achadh mhòr, a village near the house on the eastern road, in the roof of the village shrine.

events.title: Seònaid's house
events.body: An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, the carters' house on the coal road that Seònaid Bhàn opened again in the early years of the digging, is kept now by her great-grandson Aonghas. It is the busiest of the walled houses, the one the constables search most often and find least in.

events.title: The first stoppage together
events.body: For the first time the mining country stops work on one day in many places at once. Scattered as it is, the resistance of the Dia-thìrich can act as one when it chooses.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fire on Cnoc an Rabhaidh

events.title: Muileann bheag in the north-east
events.body: The workings at Muileann bheag in the north-east, among the druid villages, stop with the rest. The town's custodian writes that it is the first thing the town has done with the hills in a hundred years.

events.title: The northern pits at Àth dhomhain
events.body: The pits north of the hills at Àth dhomhain stop with the rest on the day of the stoppage, the word brought by a runner and not by the beacon. Their crew-leaders are among those shipped over the sea.

events.title: Ceann bheag stops
events.body: The coal stage at Ceann bheag on the northern coast stops loading the same day. Its dockers had not been told; they stop because the coal stops coming.

events.title: The quarrymen of Cnoc gheal
events.body: The quarrymen of Cnoc gheal in the north-east, who cut stone for the Company's buildings, lay down their tools on the day of the stoppage unasked. Why, no one says.

events.title: The day the pits stopped
events.body: On the day of the stoppage every working in the Muileann chrom district halted at once, and with them Baile thais, Cnoc chaol, the silver town and the eastern pits at Ros fhionn. The sign was a beacon fire lit on the hills above Doire mhòr, which the Company took for a heath fire.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fire on Cnoc an Rabhaidh

events.title: The coal ships wait
events.body: The Company's steamships lie six days at Ros dhomhain with empty holds. The agents at the quay write that they have never seen the harbour so quiet, and that it frightened them more than the crowds.

events.title: The stoppage broken
events.body: The stoppage ends when the constables shut the Company stores in every district at once. Forty crew-leaders are taken; thirty-two are let go without charge, and eight are shipped over the sea to an Tìr Thall for trial and never heard of again.

events.title: The fire on Cnoc an Rabhaidh
events.body: On 27 am Màrt, Aonghas watches smoke rise thin from Cnoc an Rabhaidh in a hard north-west wind, and every wheel within sight of his yard stops within the hour. A carter in his own yard names it a heath fire before anyone learns otherwise.

links.title: The first stoppage together

links.title: The day the pits stopped

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beacon hill at Doire mhòr
