told_in.section: IV. Of the Fire Taken for Heath

events.title: Beacon hill at Doire mhòr
events.body: Doire mhòr, which refused the first contract and then lost its water, has by now but a few households. The beacon of the stoppage was lit on its hill by the children's children of Beathag Dhubh's people, and the constables burn the heather of the hill to deny it to them.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The fire on Cnoc an Rabhaidh

events.title: Fewer ships from over the sea
events.body: The keepers' daybooks at the five beacons show fewer ships from an Tìr Thall each year, and the ships that come are older. The Company's letters speak of troubles at home and do not say what they are.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Buabhall's word on a house with nothing left to guard

events.title: Caol leathan's idle harbour
events.body: At Caol leathan the wool for the humans' market waits for room in ships that do not come. The merchants of the town begin to sell their wool inland again by barter, against the law.

events.title: Caol bheag's empty quay
events.body: The Company's quay at Caol bheag on the northern coast, built for the eastern trade, sees one ship in a season. The Company's agent there writes that he has been forgotten.

events.title: Tormod Buabhall's word on a house with nothing left to guard
events.body: Meeting Aonghas at the horse-fair after the ships have thinned to nothing, Tormod Buabhall tells him a house with no custom left keeps its gates shut for a different reason than before: a house that guards everything still has, behind its locked door, something it means to keep.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fewer ships from over the sea

told_in.book: Of the Houses on the Roads
told_in.section: I. Of the House at the Halfway Stage

events.title: Leave no longer asked
events.body: The humans' Administration begins to give commands without seeking the counsel of the Dia-thìrich at all. The pretence of leave asked and given is dropped.

events.title: Lionel Strake Commissioner
events.body: Charles Merriman leaves Dia-thìr in ill health, and Lionel Strake, a soldier, comes after him. His commission, read aloud at the Residency, makes no mention of the Council of Custodians, and he does not call on it.

events.title: The council locked out
events.body: Strake has the council hall at Cathair dhearg locked and its keys lodged at the Residency. The custodians meet instead in Macha's temple, whose priests, who had blessed the humans' coin, now shelter those who petitioned against it.

events.title: The iron bird
events.body: Strake brings a flying machine from an Tìr Thall in the hold of a Company steamship and has it flown from a field above the Residency over the coal country, to count the workings from the air. The Dia-thìrich call it eun-iarainn, the iron bird. The custodians enter it in the roll as the first thing seen over Dia-thìr that flew and was not alive.

events.title: The edict of seizure
events.body: The humans' Administration claims the right to take any dwelling of the Dia-thìrich it deems needful for the widening of the workings. Of all the grievances it is the one most often named in every surviving account of what followed.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The old man of Doire mhòr

events.title: The seizure of Doire mhòr
events.body: The first dwellings taken under the edict are those of Doire mhòr, for a new shaft beneath the hill, and constables carry out the last households. The village that refused the first contract is the first emptied by the last.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The old man of Doire mhòr

events.title: Evictions at Baile dhomhain
events.body: At Baile dhomhain, the first camp laid out on paper, two streets are pulled down for a spoil-tip. The families are offered huts at Àth ìseal and marks for their timber; most go to kin in the hill villages instead.

events.title: The old man of Doire mhòr
events.body: An old man carried gently from his own doorstone by constables clearing houses under the edict of seizure asks only that it be written down that they were gentle about it. Mòrag nic Iain Maor, come from Muileann chrom, carries the sentence home with no book to hand.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The edict of seizure

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The seizure of Doire mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Breaking of the Staff
told_in.section: II. Of the Edict of Seizure

events.title: Mòrag Maor lays down the staff
events.body: Mòrag nic Iain Maor, fourth of her line to hold the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, will not carry out evictions in her district, and breaks the staff at the Company's door. Three other overseers give up their places in the same month, and the Company puts humans in them.

events.title: The silver guild arms
events.body: The silver guild of Muileann chiar, still holding its seam under the compact of a century before, begins to buy rifles through the eastern pirates. Its ledger enters them as refining tools.

events.title: Rifles by way of the pirates
events.body: The silver guild's rifles come ashore from the raiders' boats in the eastern waters, where no Company gunboat has sailed for years. The raiders take their pay in bar silver, by weight.

events.title: The council in the forest of Cnoc bheag
events.body: Custodians, crew-leaders of the Lamp-Watch and the dissenting priests of Macha meet in the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag and make one council for the mining country, and choose Eilidh nic Raghnaill to speak for it. No human writing records the meeting.

events.title: The order to seize
events.body: Strake orders the taking of Eilidh nic Raghnaill and the members of the forest council. The constables go to Baile thais and find the house empty and the town silent.

events.title: War
events.body: The Dia-thìrich, acting together across the whole mining country for the first time, pass from grievance to open war.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach Ruadh's ride of the twenty-eighth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The beacons of the coal country answer

events.title: Coinneach Ruadh's ride of the twenty-eighth
events.body: Coinneach Ruadh rides into Muileann chrom on the twenty-eighth of an Gearran with word that the grievance is called across every mining district at once, and that the Residency has already had its answer that morning from Muileann chrom and Baile thais both.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: War

told_in.book: Of the Breaking of the Staff
told_in.section: V. Of the Silent Town

events.title: The beacons of the coal country answer
events.body: On the night war is called, signal fires long kept secret are carried openly to every beacon height the mining districts hold, ridge answering ridge from Doire mhòr to the silver hills, the first time the whole coal country has shown itself lit at once.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: War

told_in.book: Of the Breaking of the Staff
told_in.section: V. Of the Silent Town

events.title: The stores taken at Muileann chrom
events.body: The war opens in the hills. At Muileann chrom crews under Mòrag nic Iain rush the walled store at first light, and its eleven constables yield without a shot. The rifles and the grain of the store are carried off before noon.

events.title: The quay at Ceann fhada seized
events.body: Crews from the camps take the Company's coal quay at Ceann fhada and sink two barges across its mouth. No coal leaves the hills by water again in this age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pàdraig Reamhar scuttles his own barge

events.title: Pàdraig Reamhar scuttles his own barge
events.body: The boatman Pàdraig Reamhar, who built the larger of the two barges sunk at Ceann fhada with his own father twenty years before, knocks the plugs from her hull with his own hands and says afterward only that she had been a good boat.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The quay at Ceann fhada seized

told_in.book: Of the Rising in the Hills
told_in.section: I. Of the First Light at Muileann chrom

events.title: The siege of the store at Baile thais
events.body: At Baile thais the constables hold their walled pithead against the town for eleven days, as long as the first strike a lifetime before, and yield on the twelfth when their water fails. Eilidh nic Raghnaill sends them under guard to the coast unharmed. The Residency did not look for such mercy, and did not return it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The boy of Baile thais shows the wall

events.title: The crews meet on the moor
events.body: Crew-leaders of Baile gharbh and the other northern pits meet by night on the moor above Cnoc naomh and fix the week of their rising. Each brings a stone of spoil from his own pit, and the stones are left in a cairn. The place is called Coinneachadh a' Mhonaidh, the meeting of the moor.

events.title: The northern pits rise
events.body: The crews at Baile gharbh and the northern pits rise in the same week, take the constable posts at Muileann shean and Tobar ghorm, and send the constables south on foot.

events.title: The coal road cut
events.body: Aonghas, keeper of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, shuts the gates of the house across the coal road, and the men in its loft come down armed. The road between the capital and the hills is cut at its half-way stage, and stays cut.

events.title: Uilleam Gobha's forge
events.body: At Muileann dhearg the smith Uilleam Gobha makes the Company's own blasting-powder into grenades cased in tin from the coal sheds, and forges pike-heads from rails torn up in the galleries. The rebels' council writes that without him it could not have fought its first season.

events.title: The capital rises
events.body: At Cathair dhearg the custodians break the Residency's locks on their council hall and sit in it again. The townsfolk hold Drochaid Cathair dhearg against the constables sent up from the harbour, and barricade the bridge built for the coal-carts with the carts themselves.

events.title: Cathair dhomhain joins
events.body: At Cathair dhomhain the townsfolk break open the Company's warehouse, the first building on Dia-thìr the Company ever owned, and carry off its tools for the council's companies.

events.title: Muileann mhin takes sides
events.body: At Muileann mhin, a river port just east of the capital, the townsfolk argue for three days, and then send boats to the council. Through the winter the boats carry food down the Abhainn fhionn to the capital.

events.title: The Residency fortified
events.body: Lionel Strake draws the Administration back into the Residency above Ros dhomhain and fortifies the Company's quarter of the harbour. The city below, Dia-thìrich almost to a man, neither joins the rising nor withstands it, and the constables do not trust it enough to leave the walls.

events.title: The fight at the ford of Àth chiar
events.body: A column of constables and Company guards under Major Peter Ashdown marches up the coal road to relieve the hills, and is met at the ford of Àth chiar, where the rebels hold the far bank. Ashdown loses forty men and his baggage and turns back. The rebels lose nineteen, and the council's roll names them all.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The turnip cart to the ford

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The nineteen of Àth chiar buried

events.title: The turnip cart to the ford
events.body: A cart with a false floor of turnips carries Uilleam Gobha's grenades up the cut coal road to the crews waiting at the ford of Àth chiar, the first of his work to leave Muileann dhearg for open fighting.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fight at the ford of Àth chiar

told_in.book: Of the Rising in the Hills
told_in.section: V. Of the Ford of Àth chiar

events.title: The nineteen of Àth chiar buried
events.body: The council's clerk Fionnuala writes down by lamp-light the names of the nineteen dead of Àth chiar and reads the list aloud the next morning; within the week they are buried on the moor above Cnoc naomh, within sight of the cairn raised there before the fighting began.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fight at the ford of Àth chiar

told_in.book: Of the Rising in the Hills
told_in.section: V. Of the Ford of Àth chiar

events.title: Ashdown's retreat through Dùn chrom
events.body: Ashdown's column falls back through Dùn chrom and lies a night at the barracks there. In the morning the town has shut its gates behind them, and the column goes on to the coast without its wounded, whom the townsfolk keep and nurse.

events.title: The silver town rises
events.body: The silver guild of Muileann chiar declares for the council and opens its armoury, and the Company's agents in the town are escorted to the coast with their papers. The guild's ledger notes that here alone the rising took nothing, for the humans had never held anything there to take.

events.title: The surrender at Dùn ìseal
events.body: The small constable post at Dùn ìseal, cut off by the rising at the silver town, yields to the silver guild's riflemen after a single exchange of fire. The east of the island is clear of human arms.

events.title: Dùn dhearg declares
events.body: The custodians of Dùn dhearg declare for the council and send it grain. Theirs is the town whose custodian wrote the only surviving defence of the Small-Burning Law, and their declaration quotes it.

events.title: Cnoc leathan's riflemen
events.body: Riflemen raised at Cnoc leathan in the east join the silver guild's companies and hold the eastern road. The Company's carters on the road are let go home with their carts.

events.title: The eastern pits at Ros fhionn
events.body: The crews of the eastern workings about Ros fhionn stop the pumps and walk out, and the lower galleries flood. The Company's engineers there go down the Abhainn chaol and take ship at Seann Mhorn for Ros dhomhain. The bridge on the eastern coal road falls silent.

events.title: Seann Toll shelled
events.body: A Company steamship comes up the Abhainn uaine and shells the coal stage at Seann Toll to deny it to the rebels, and sets the fishing town behind it burning. Twenty-three townsfolk die. For the first time the humans turn the island's own coal, burning in their boilers, against a town of the Dia-thìrich.

events.title: The Leaden Hawk company
events.body: At An Cupa Dàna, the inn at Cuan dhearg, seven hawk-faithful crewmen of the river towns wait nine hours for the council's letters to the Hawk coast, and leave with them at dark. Each wears a hawk cast in lead from the cartridges taken at the store at Muileann chrom, and they are called Buidheann an t-Seabhaig Luaidhe, the Leaden Hawk company.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach Beag puts his name forward

events.title: The Leaden Hawk walks to the Hawk coast
events.body: The company goes on foot and lightly laden: past the burned stage at Seann Toll, through Baile thais, over the hills by Achadh dhomhain and Cuan bheag, down the Abhainn ìseal by Ceann òg and Inis ìseal to Cnoc bheag, and along the Hawk coast by Inis bhàn, Ros gheal and Seann Skell to Inis mhin, some fifty-five miles in a little over two days. At every hawk-house on the way they read the council's letter aloud, and at Seann Skell they leave it with Ìomhar Seabhag.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The letter read at a nameless hawk-house

events.title: Rumours at Inis mhin
events.body: At Inis mhin, the northern landing the humans had walled, the company lies twelve hours in a boat-shed and hears that Strake's constables ride the western roads out of Ros bheag every day. They hire a carriage of a carter of the town and leave the roads altogether.

events.title: The watch in the grasslands
events.body: A day and a half by carriage across country, off every road, brings the company to the grasslands above Tobar dhomhain in the western hills. They lie eleven hours in the long grass above the road from Ros bheag to the northern concession and count the constables' riders who pass. Their own list gives forty-one riders, none of them going north.

events.title: The Leaden Hawk at Inis thais
events.body: A day and a half more by carriage, still off the roads, brings the company down to Inis thais, six days after it left Cuan dhearg. The priests of Òrd na Cloiche hear the council's letter in the temple of the Stone. They will send no men, but they shut the harbour of Inis thais to the Company's ships and give the hawk-faithful the use of the Fianna's roads. There the Leaden Hawk's road ends, and its seven join the hawk company when it is mustered at the western Seann Skell.

events.title: Coaling from Inis mhòr
events.body: The Company's steamships take their fuel from the coal stacked on the quays of Inis mhòr, the river port just east of the capital, whose barges carry it down the Abhainn fhionn to the ships at Cathair dhomhain. The townsfolk set the stacks alight. The ships put in at Ros dhomhain instead, and burn their own stores.

events.title: The fishermen of Seann Chwen
events.body: Fishing boats of Seann Chwen and Ros ruadh, sailing by night along the south coast, board a Company coaster at anchor and burn her. The Company draws its coastal shipping back to the harbours of Ros dhomhain and Ros bheag.

events.title: The other Seann Chwen
events.body: The fishermen of the other Seann Chwen, further west on the south coast, join the raids along the shore. The rolls tell the two towns apart by the names of their boats.

events.title: Cathair gheal behind its walls
events.body: The human town of Cathair gheal in the northern concession shuts its gates and raises a militia, but sends none of it south to the Residency. Its magistrate writes to both sides asking to be left alone. The council grants it; Strake does not answer.

events.title: Muileann àrsaidh closes its road
events.body: Muileann àrsaidh, a town of the concession, blocks its road with carts and keeps a watch on it against both sides. No one attacks it. The watch is kept to the end of the war.

events.title: The hawk-shrines open
events.body: From the shrine at Seann Skell Ìomhar Seabhag declares that the war is Mòd's own hunger turned back on those who fed it. The hawk-shrines of the west become mustering houses, and a company of the hawk-faithful marches south to join the council.

events.title: The hawk company at Seann Skell
events.body: The company of the hawk-faithful is mustered at Seann Skell, the western city, a short march north-east of the human port of Ros bheag. It holds the road between Ros bheag and the north-west for the rest of the war.

events.title: The southern beacon dark
events.body: The keepers at Tobar dhearg put out the beacon, and the keepers at Àth dhearg and Baile ìseal do the same. Company ships feeling their way along the coast by night run on the reefs the beacons were built to light, and two are lost.

events.title: No relief from over the sea
events.body: The Administration's letter-books ask again and again for troops and ships from an Tìr Thall. In the whole first year of the war one ship comes, with dispatches and a few crates of cartridges, and sails again within the week.

events.title: The lines at midsummer
events.body: The lines stand at midsummer where the first winter of the war left them: the council holds the hills, the east and the capital; Strake holds the Residency, the harbour quarter below it, and the western ports. Neither side has the strength to attack the other.

events.title: Grain from Seann Warr
events.body: Seann Warr, the farming town in the south-east and not the salt port of that name in the west, has sent grain to the hills by the eastern roads since the winter. The council's roll lists the carts.

events.title: Hunger in the capital
events.body: Its harbour held by the Residency, Cathair dhearg has gone short since the winter. The custodians share out the grain by household, and the roll records that they took the same share as everyone else.

events.title: The burning of the tithe-books
events.body: In three raids the rebels destroy the tithe ledgers of the humans' Administration. Later chroniclers make much of it; it did little.

events.title: The counting-house at Ros dhomhain
events.body: The first raid was on the Company's counting-house at the Ros dhomhain quay, within the lines. Men of the harbour quarter under Dùghall Dubh came in over the roofs, carried the tithe books into the yard and burned them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The night clerk of the counting-house is taken without a blow

events.title: The night clerk of the counting-house is taken without a blow
events.body: The counting-house's night clerk is found sitting on its steps in his shirt with his hands laced over his head before the raiders reach the ground floor, and Dùghall Dubh judges, from the look of him, that some part of the man had waited a year for the night to come.

links.title: The counting-house at Ros dhomhain

told_in.section: II. Of the Roofs in Stocking Feet

events.title: The tithe-house at Ceann àrsaidh
events.body: The second raid burned the Administration's tithe-house at Ceann àrsaidh, where the share owed by every settlement in the hills had been entered since the first schedule. The clerks were let go. The custodians of Ceann àrsaidh asked that one ledger be spared for the record, and their own people refused them.

events.title: The weigh-house at Muileann chrom
events.body: The third raid burned the Company's weigh-house at Muileann chrom with its steelyard ledgers, where the coal of the hills had been entered by the ton since the first contract. The rebels' own chronicler writes that the fire burned green.

events.title: The fight at Cnoc ghorm
events.body: Company guards and constables sallying from the capital's harbour to win back the eastern road are driven back at Cnoc ghorm, in the hills beyond the capital. It is the Administration's last attempt in the war to reach the mining district.

events.title: The harbour quarter changes sides
events.body: After the raid on the counting-house the Dia-thìrich of the Ros dhomhain harbour quarter open the lower gates to the council's companies, and Strake is left holding only the Residency and the Company's quays. The same night men of the quarter burn the Company's flying machine in its shed above the town. It had not flown since the war began, for want of the spirit its engine burned, and nothing has flown over Dia-thìr since that was not a bird.

events.title: Cuan uaine opens its quays
events.body: The river quays of Cuan uaine, east of the capital, open to the council's boats. With them and the harbour quarter of Ros dhomhain both lost, the Residency can be fed only by water, up the Abhainn gheal from the sea.

events.title: Strake forsakes the Residency
events.body: Lionel Strake leaves the Residency by water, down the Abhainn gheal, with his officers, the Mission's clergy and the Company's agents, and takes the Administration to Ros bheag. The council's companies enter the Residency the next morning and find it stripped of all but its furniture.

links.title: The letter-books found whole at the Residency

links.title: Prentice the counting-house clerk goes down the river

events.title: The letter-books found whole at the Residency
events.body: Where Strake has taken plate and account-papers down the river by night, Dùghall Dubh finds a room of the Residency's letter-books left standing untouched on an unlocked shelf, thirty years of the Administration's own correspondence with an Tìr Thall, and sends word of it to the council's clerks that evening.

events.title: Prentice the counting-house clerk goes down the river
events.body: Dùghall Dubh learns from a clerk taken at the Residency that Prentice, who weighed coal beside him nine years at the counting-house scales, went down the river with Strake's household the night the Residency fell, leaving the ledgers he had kept behind as ash.

events.title: Ros bheag the last seat
events.body: At Ros bheag, the western port the humans had used since the early years, Strake sets up what is left of the Administration. The human families of the west and south, a few thousand in all, gather behind its walls.

events.title: Outposts at Ros àrsaidh
events.body: Strake posts constables at Ros àrsaidh, north of Ros bheag, to hold the coast road, Ceum Ros àrsaidh. The townsfolk bring them food and news, and the news is always a day old.

events.title: Hunger in Ros bheag
events.body: The roads cut and no ships coming from over the sea, Ros bheag runs short of food within months. By Strake's order the Company's stores are opened to the human families and the Dia-thìrich townsfolk alike, the one deed of his the Dia-thìrich rolls give him credit for.

events.title: Cuan shean refuses the humans
events.body: The custodians of Cuan shean, where the first humans came ashore, shut its harbour to Company ships. The council's roll sets it down and says no more.

events.title: The families of Baile dhìreach
events.body: At Baile dhìreach each side asks the children of the old joint council, many of them of both peoples, which they are. Most of them, it is written, would not answer, and neither side made them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh Hale will not choose

events.title: The last ship from the east
events.body: The last ship known to come from an Tìr Thall anchors at Ros bheag at Samhain. She brings no troops and no grain, only a sealed letter for the Commissioner, and sails again on the next tide with as many passengers as she can hold.

events.title: The truce of Àth àrsaidh
events.body: Envoys of the council and of the Administration meet at Àth àrsaidh, on the edge of the northern concession, and agree a truce: the humans left on Dia-thìr shall withdraw into the north-west under the council's safe-conduct, and the council shall leave the towns of the concession standing.

events.title: Baile Mòr ruadh receives the columns
events.body: The truce names Baile Mòr ruadh, the greatest town of the north-west, as the place where the columns will be received. Its Dia-thìrich folk are given the choice of staying or going south. The roll gives the numbers of each, and they are close.

events.title: The columns go north
events.body: The human families of Ros bheag, Cuan shean, Baile dhìreach and the south-west march north along the western roads under guard of the council's companies. Few of them had ever lived in the north. The roll records that no column was attacked, and none was helped.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Hannah Webb walks north

events.title: The columns at Àth chrom
events.body: The columns cross the ford at Àth chrom on their way north. The custodians of the town stand at the ford and count them over, and it is the last count the Dia-thìrich make of the humans on Dia-thìr in this age.

events.title: Àth leathan
events.body: At Àth leathan, the last stage before the northern country, the columns camp for a night. The custodians of the town write that the humans asked the name of the place, and that several of them wrote it down.

events.title: The ship that sailed east
events.body: Lionel Strake, the last Commissioner, sails from Cuan shean for an Tìr Thall with his officers in the last ship on the island able to make the crossing. The keeper at Taigh-solais Baile chrom sets down her passing in his daybook. Nothing on Dia-thìr tells of her coming anywhere.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keys given up at Cuan shean

events.title: The beacons relit
events.body: The council orders the five beacons lit again, from Baile chrom round to Tobar dhearg. The keepers' daybooks, which had counted human ships since the ring was finished, are still kept, with nothing in them.

events.title: The rolls sent to Muileann chaol
events.body: The custodians send what survives of the rolls of the age, their copies of the petitions, the book of Baile thais and the letter-books left in the Residency, to the cellars at Muileann chaol. What the Administration's own clerks carried west with Strake is not known.

events.title: Coinneach Beag puts his name forward
events.body: When the crew-leaders of the river towns ask for seven men who can keep their feet on a hill road and hold their tongues, Coinneach Beag, a boatman of Cuan dhearg raised on the river since boyhood and no stranger to the Company's rule over his own family, puts his name forward before he has properly decided to.

events.title: The letter read at a nameless hawk-house
events.body: On the road past Seann Toll, Coinneach Beag reads the council's letter aloud in a bare hawk-house of six benches, his voice unsteady at first; an old woman by the fire answers only that it has come to that, and no one else speaks.

events.title: The boy of Baile thais shows the wall
events.body: Passing through Baile thais, the Leaden Hawk company is shown by a boy of nine or ten the marks on the store's outer wall from the siege's eleven days, told with more pride than fear, the town's memory of its own fight already settling into telling.

events.title: Eilidh Hale will not choose
events.body: Asked on the steps of the council hall at Baile dhìreach which people she is, Eilidh Hale, who has kept the joint council's books three winters running, answers only that she keeps the books, and no more. She is neither pressed further nor turned away, and stays in the town through the rest of the war.

events.title: Hannah Webb walks north
events.body: Hannah Webb, who keeps her vigil behind Baile chrom and nursed at Cathair gheal through the fever, walks out to meet the columns at the concession's southern edge and walks back north with them, an old woman of the last families out of Cuan shean on her arm who will not be carried.

events.title: The keys given up at Cuan shean
events.body: The harbour officers of Ceann mhòr, Cathair gheal and Inis àrsaidh ride two days south with their towns' chests of harbour keys and set them at Strake's feet on the quay at Cuan shean before his ship sails, saying only that the accounts are even and that who wants the keys after is not theirs to decide. Strake takes the chests aboard with him.

events.title: The Severance
events.body: The war ends, and the crossing itself is shut: whatever way let the humans reach Dia-thìr closes. The humans still on the island are led into the northern country that their children's children hold to this day. Cian and Lorccan, not yet twenty, grow up in the wake of it.
